345: **[ARTICLE 5 --- TERM AND TERMINATION]{.underline}**
346: 
347: **Section 5.1** *Initial Term.* This Agreement shall become effective on the Closing Date and shall continue for a period of eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date (the \"**Initial Term**\"), unless earlier terminated in accordance with this Article 5. For the avoidance of doubt, this Agreement shall have no force or effect unless and until the Closing occurs under the Purchase Agreement.
348: 
349: **Section 5.2** *Automatic Renewal.* Upon expiration of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive six (6)-month periods (each, a \"**Renewal Term**\"), unless Service Provider delivers written notice of non-renewal to Service Recipient at least one hundred twenty (120) days prior to the expiration of the then-current Initial Term or Renewal Term, as applicable. The Agreement may be renewed for up to two (2) successive Renewal Terms pursuant to this Section 5.2. During any Renewal Term, all terms and conditions of this Agreement shall continue in full force and effect, including the Fees set forth on the Fee Schedule, subject to any adjustments expressly provided for herein. For the avoidance of doubt, the burden of providing notice of non-renewal rests solely with Service Provider; failure by Service Provider to deliver timely notice of non-renewal shall result in automatic renewal for the next succeeding Renewal Term (subject to the two (2) Renewal Term maximum).
350: 
351: **Section 5.3** *Termination of Individual Services.* Either Party may terminate any individual Service upon not less than one hundred twenty (120) days\' prior written notice to the other Party, provided that such notice specifies in reasonable detail the Service to be terminated and the effective date of termination. Termination of an individual Service shall not affect the continuance of any other Service being provided under this Agreement. Upon termination of any individual Service, the corresponding Fees for such Service shall cease to accrue as of the effective date of such termination.
352: 
353: **Section 5.4** *Termination for Cause.* Either Party may terminate this Agreement in whole, or with respect to any individual Service, upon written notice to the other Party if the other Party materially breaches any provision of this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within thirty (30) days after receipt of written notice from the non-breaching Party specifying the nature of the breach in reasonable detail. If the breach is of such a nature that it cannot reasonably be cured within thirty (30) days, the breaching Party shall not be deemed in default so long as it commences cure within such thirty (30)-day period and thereafter diligently prosecutes such cure to completion; provided, however, that no cure period shall extend beyond ninety (90) days from the date of the initial notice of breach.
354: 
355: **Section 5.5** *Effect of Termination.* Upon termination or expiration of any Service or of this Agreement (in whole or in part):
356: 
357: > \(a\) Service Provider\'s obligation to provide the terminated or expired Services shall immediately cease as of the effective date of such termination or expiration;
358: >
359: > \(b\) Service Recipient shall pay to Service Provider all accrued but unpaid Fees and expenses for Services actually performed through the effective date of termination or expiration, which payment shall be made within thirty (30) days following the effective date of termination or expiration;
360: >
361: > \(c\) each Party shall promptly return to the other Party, or at the other Party\'s election destroy and certify in writing the destruction of, all Confidential Information of the other Party that relates to the terminated or expired Services, except to the extent that retention is required by Applicable Law or bona fide document retention policies (in which case such retained Confidential Information shall remain subject to the confidentiality obligations of Article 8); and
362: >
363: > \(d\) all rights and obligations of the Parties with respect to the terminated or expired Services shall cease, except as expressly provided in Section 5.6 (Survival).
364: 
365: **Section 5.6** *Survival.* The provisions of Article 1 (Definitions), Article 7 (Intellectual Property), Article 8 (Confidentiality), Article 9 (Indemnification), Article 10 (Limitation of Liability), Article 11 (Representations and Warranties), Article 13 (Insurance), Article 14 (Audit Rights), and Article 15 (General Provisions) shall survive the termination or expiration of this Agreement in accordance with their respective terms.
366: 
367: **[ARTICLE 6 --- FEES AND PAYMENT]{.underline}**
368: 
369: **Section 6.1** *Service Charges.* In consideration for the provision of the Services, Service Recipient shall pay to Service Provider the Fees set forth on the Fee Schedule (Schedule G) for each Service during the Term. The Fees for each Service category are calculated on a cost-plus basis reflecting Service Provider\'s fully-loaded cost of providing the applicable Service (including personnel costs, allocated overhead, and systems costs), plus a markup as set forth on the Fee Schedule. The Fees represent the sole compensation to which Service Provider is entitled for the provision of the Services, and Service Provider shall not charge Service Recipient for any internal costs, overhead, or administrative expenses except as expressly reflected in the Fee Schedule.
370: 
371: **Section 6.2** *Invoicing.* Service Provider shall deliver to Service Recipient a monthly invoice within fifteen (15) Business Days after the end of each calendar month, setting forth in reasonable detail the Services performed during such month, the applicable FTE hours, and the Fees due for such month. Each invoice shall be accompanied by such supporting documentation as Service Recipient may reasonably request to verify the accuracy of the amounts invoiced. Invoices shall be delivered to the attention of Service Recipient\'s Service Manager for the applicable Service category, with a copy to Service Recipient\'s Chief Financial Officer.
372: 
373: **Section 6.3** *Payment.* Service Recipient shall pay each undisputed invoice within a commercially reasonable time following receipt thereof. All payments shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated by Service Provider in writing from time to time.
374: 
375: **Section 6.4** *Fee Escalation.* The Fees set forth on the Fee Schedule are fixed for the duration of the Term and shall not be subject to escalation or adjustment, except as expressly provided in this Agreement.
376: 
377: **Section 6.5** *Taxes.* All Fees stated in this Agreement and on the Fee Schedule are exclusive of any applicable sales, use, value-added, goods and services, or similar Taxes (collectively, \"**Transaction Taxes**\"). Service Recipient shall be responsible for and shall pay, or reimburse Service Provider for, all Transaction Taxes imposed on or with respect to the Services, other than Taxes measured by Service Provider\'s net income, capital, or franchise. Service Provider shall separately state any Transaction Taxes on its invoices. Each Party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to minimize Transaction Taxes and shall cooperate in good faith with the other Party to obtain any available exemptions or reduced rates for such Taxes.
378: 
379: **Section 6.6** *Disputed Amounts.* If Service Recipient disputes any amount set forth on an invoice in good faith, Service Recipient shall: (a) pay the undisputed portion of such invoice when due in accordance with Section 6.3; (b) provide written notice to Service Provider of the disputed amount, specifying in reasonable detail the basis for the dispute, within fifteen (15) Business Days after receipt of the applicable invoice; and (c) work in good faith with Service Provider to resolve the dispute within thirty (30) days after such notice. If the Parties are unable to resolve the dispute within such thirty (30)-day period, either Party may escalate the matter to the Steering Committee. Pending resolution of any disputed amount, Service Provider shall continue to perform the Services without interruption.
380: 
381: **[ARTICLE 7 --- INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY]{.underline}**
382: 
383: **Section 7.1** *Service Provider Materials --- License Grant.* Service Provider hereby grants to Service Recipient a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid-up, non-exclusive license to use, reproduce, modify, adapt, and create derivative works of any Service Provider Materials (including any tools, methodologies, templates, processes, software, or know-how) developed or utilized by Service Provider in connection with the performance of the Services under this Agreement. This license shall include the right to sublicense to Service Recipient\'s Affiliates, successors, and assigns, and shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason. For the avoidance of doubt, the foregoing license extends to all Service Provider Materials that are used, in whole or in part, in the delivery of any of the Services, regardless of whether such Service Provider Materials were created specifically for the Services or existed prior to the Effective Date and were adapted or applied in the course of service delivery. Nothing in this Section 7.1 shall be construed to transfer ownership of any Service Provider Materials to Service Recipient; Service Provider retains all right, title, and interest in and to the Service Provider Materials, subject to the license granted herein.
384: 
385: **Section 7.2** *Service Recipient Materials.* Service Recipient retains all right, title, and interest in and to any data, materials, information, documents, or other content provided by Service Recipient to Service Provider for purposes of the Services (collectively, \"**Service Recipient Materials**\"). Service Provider shall use the Service Recipient Materials solely for the purpose of performing the Services under this Agreement and for no other purpose. Upon termination or expiration of any Service or this Agreement, Service Provider shall promptly return or, at Service Recipient\'s election, destroy all Service Recipient Materials in its possession or control.
386: 
387: **Section 7.3** *Feedback.* To the extent that Service Recipient provides any suggestions, ideas, enhancement requests, recommendations, or other feedback to Service Provider regarding the Service Provider Materials or any other intellectual property of Service Provider (collectively, \"**Feedback**\"), Service Recipient hereby assigns to Service Provider all right, title, and interest in and to such Feedback and agrees that Service Provider is free to use, disclose, reproduce, license, and otherwise distribute and exploit such Feedback as it sees fit, without obligation or restriction of any kind. Service Recipient acknowledges that this assignment is irrevocable and that no additional consideration is required.
388: 
389: **[ARTICLE 8 --- CONFIDENTIALITY]{.underline}**
390: 
391: **Section 8.1** *Confidentiality Obligations.* Each Party agrees to hold the other Party\'s Confidential Information in strict confidence and to protect such Confidential Information using the same degree of care that it uses to protect its own confidential information of like kind, but in no event less than a reasonable degree of care. Neither Party shall disclose the other Party\'s Confidential Information to any Person, except to its Representatives who have a bona fide need to know such information for the purpose of performing obligations or exercising rights under this Agreement and who are bound by written confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth in this Article 8. Each Party shall be responsible for any breach of this Article 8 by its Representatives. Neither Party shall use the other Party\'s Confidential Information for any purpose other than in connection with the performance of its obligations or the exercise of its rights under this Agreement. Without limiting the foregoing, neither Party shall reverse engineer, decompile, or disassemble any Confidential Information of the other Party.
392: 
393: **Section 8.2** *Exceptions.* The obligations set forth in Section 8.1 shall not apply to any information that:
394: 
395: > \(a\) is or becomes publicly available other than as a result of a disclosure by the Receiving Party or its Representatives in breach of this Agreement;
396: >
397: > \(b\) was already known to the Receiving Party at the time of disclosure by the Disclosing Party, as evidenced by competent written records of the Receiving Party;
398: >
399: > \(c\) is independently developed by the Receiving Party without use of or reference to the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information, as evidenced by competent written records of the Receiving Party; or
400: >
401: > \(d\) is received by the Receiving Party from a third party who is not, to the Receiving Party\'s knowledge, bound by any obligation of confidentiality with respect to such information.
402: 
403: In addition, the Receiving Party may disclose the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information to the extent required by Applicable Law, regulation, or order of a Governmental Authority, or by the rules and regulations of a stock exchange on which the Receiving Party\'s (or its parent\'s) securities are listed; provided that the Receiving Party shall, to the extent legally permissible, provide prompt written notice to the Disclosing Party of such required disclosure so as to enable the Disclosing Party to seek a protective order or other appropriate remedy. If a protective order or other remedy is not obtained, the Receiving Party shall disclose only that portion of the Confidential Information that it is legally required to disclose and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain reliable assurance that confidential treatment will be given to such disclosed information.
404: 
405: **Section 8.3** *Survival of Confidentiality.* The confidentiality obligations set forth in this Article 8 shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement for a period of three (3) years following the effective date of such expiration or termination.
406: 
407: **Section 8.4** *Data Privacy.* Each Party shall comply with all applicable data privacy and data protection laws of the United States in connection with its performance under this Agreement, including with respect to the collection, use, processing, storage, transfer, and disposal of any personally identifiable information of employees, customers, or other individuals. Each Party shall implement and maintain appropriate technical and organizational measures to protect personal data against unauthorized access, use, disclosure, alteration, or destruction.
408: 
409: **[ARTICLE 9 --- INDEMNIFICATION]{.underline}**
410: 
411: **Section 9.1** *Service Recipient Indemnification.* Service Recipient shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Service Provider and its Affiliates, and their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, successors, and assigns (each, a \"**Service Provider Indemnitee**\") from and against any and all Losses incurred or suffered by any Service Provider Indemnitee arising out of or relating to:
412: 
413: > \(a\) Service Recipient\'s use of or reliance on the Services or the results thereof;
414: >
415: > \(b\) any breach by Service Recipient of any representation, warranty, covenant, or obligation under this Agreement;
416: >
417: > \(c\) any negligent or wrongful act or omission of Service Recipient or its employees, agents, or contractors in connection with this Agreement; or
418: >
419: > \(d\) any claim by a third party arising out of Service Recipient\'s use of the Services or any deliverables provided hereunder, except to the extent such claim arises from Service Provider\'s gross negligence or willful misconduct.
420: 
421: **Section 9.2** *Service Provider Indemnification.* Service Provider shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Service Recipient and its Affiliates, and their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, successors, and assigns (each, a \"**Service Recipient Indemnitee**\") from and against any and all Losses incurred or suffered by any Service Recipient Indemnitee arising out of or relating to:
422: 
423: > \(a\) any gross negligence or willful misconduct of Service Provider, its Affiliates, or their respective employees, agents, or contractors in performing the Services;
424: >
425: > \(b\) any breach by Service Provider of any representation, warranty, covenant, or obligation under this Agreement; or
426: >

**Section 5.1** *Initial Term.* This Agreement shall become effective on the Closing Date and shall continue for a period of eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date (the \"**Initial Term**\"), unless earlier terminated in accordance with this Article 5. For the avoidance of doubt, this Agreement shall have no force or effect unless and until the Closing occurs under the Purchase Agreement.

**Section 5.2** *Automatic Renewal.* Upon expiration of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive six (6)-month periods (each, a \"**Renewal Term**\"), unless Service Provider delivers written notice of non-renewal to Service Recipient at least one hundred twenty (120) days prior to the expiration of the then-current Initial Term or Renewal Term, as applicable. The Agreement may be renewed for up to two (2) successive Renewal Terms pursuant to this Section 5.2. During any Renewal Term, all terms and conditions of this Agreement shall continue in full force and effect, including the Fees set forth on the Fee Schedule, subject to any adjustments expressly provided for herein. For the avoidance of doubt, the burden of providing notice of non-renewal rests solely with Service Provider; failure by Service Provider to deliver timely notice of non-renewal shall result in automatic renewal for the next succeeding Renewal Term (subject to the two (2) Renewal Term maximum).

**Section 5.3** *Termination of Individual Services.* Either Party may terminate any individual Service upon not less than one hundred twenty (120) days\' prior written notice to the other Party, provided that such notice specifies in reasonable detail the Service to be terminated and the effective date of termination. Termination of an individual Service shall not affect the continuance of any other Service being provided under this Agreement. Upon termination of any individual Service, the corresponding Fees for such Service shall cease to accrue as of the effective date of such termination.

**Section 5.4** *Termination for Cause.* Either Party may terminate this Agreement in whole, or with respect to any individual Service, upon written notice to the other Party if the other Party materially breaches any provision of this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within thirty (30) days after receipt of written notice from the non-breaching Party specifying the nature of the breach in reasonable detail. If the breach is of such a nature that it cannot reasonably be cured within thirty (30) days, the breaching Party shall not be deemed in default so long as it commences cure within such thirty (30)-day period and thereafter diligently prosecutes such cure to completion; provided, however, that no cure period shall extend beyond ninety (90) days from the date of the initial notice of breach.
**Section 5.5** *Effect of Termination.* Upon termination or expiration of any Service or of this Agreement (in whole or in part):
> \(a\) Service Provider\'s obligation to provide the terminated or expired Services shall immediately cease as of the effective date of such termination or expiration;

> \(b\) Service Recipient shall pay to Service Provider all accrued but unpaid Fees and expenses for Services actually performed through the effective date of termination or expiration, which payment shall be made within thirty (30) days following the effective date of termination or expiration;

> \(c\) each Party shall promptly return to the other Party, or at the other Party\'s election destroy and certify in writing the destruction of, all Confidential Information of the other Party that relates to the terminated or expired Services, except to the extent that retention is required by Applicable Law or bona fide document retention policies (in which case such retained Confidential Information shall remain subject to the confidentiality obligations of Article 8); and
> \(d\) all rights and obligations of the Parties with respect to the terminated or expired Services shall cease, except as expressly provided in Section 5.6 (Survival).

**Section 5.6** *Survival.* The provisions of Article 1 (Definitions), Article 7 (Intellectual Property), Article 8 (Confidentiality), Article 9 (Indemnification), Article 10 (Limitation of Liability), Article 11 (Representations and Warranties), Article 13 (Insurance), Article 14 (Audit Rights), and Article 15 (General Provisions) shall survive the termination or expiration of this Agreement in accordance with their respective terms.

**Section 6.1** *Service Charges.* In consideration for the provision of the Services, Service Recipient shall pay to Service Provider the Fees set forth on the Fee Schedule (Schedule G) for each Service during the Term. The Fees for each Service category are calculated on a cost-plus basis reflecting Service Provider\'s fully-loaded cost of providing the applicable Service (including personnel costs, allocated overhead, and systems costs), plus a markup as set forth on the Fee Schedule. The Fees represent the sole compensation to which Service Provider is entitled for the provision of the Services, and Service Provider shall not charge Service Recipient for any internal costs, overhead, or administrative expenses except as expressly reflected in the Fee Schedule.

**Section 6.2** *Invoicing.* Service Provider shall deliver to Service Recipient a monthly invoice within fifteen (15) Business Days after the end of each calendar month, setting forth in reasonable detail the Services performed during such month, the applicable FTE hours, and the Fees due for such month. Each invoice shall be accompanied by such supporting documentation as Service Recipient may reasonably request to verify the accuracy of the amounts invoiced. Invoices shall be delivered to the attention of Service Recipient\'s Service Manager for the applicable Service category, with a copy to Service Recipient\'s Chief Financial Officer.

**Section 6.3** *Payment.* Service Recipient shall pay each undisputed invoice within a commercially reasonable time following receipt thereof. All payments shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated by Service Provider in writing from time to time.

Service Provider shall separately state any Transaction Taxes on its invoices. Each Party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to minimize Transaction Taxes and shall cooperate in good faith with the other Party to obtain any available exemptions or reduced rates for such Taxes.

**Section 6.6** *Disputed Amounts.* If Service Recipient disputes any amount set forth on an invoice in good faith, Service Recipient shall: (a) pay the undisputed portion of such invoice when due in accordance with Section 6.3; (b) provide written notice to Service Provider of the disputed amount, specifying in reasonable detail the basis for the dispute, within fifteen (15) Business Days after receipt of the applicable invoice; and (c) work in good faith with Service Provider to resolve the dispute within thirty (30) days after such notice. > \(d\) this Agreement constitutes the legal, valid, and binding obligation of such Party, enforceable against such Party in accordance with its terms, subject to applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium, and similar laws affecting creditors\' rights generally and to general principles of equity; and

The non-affected Party shall cooperate in good faith with the affected Party\'s mitigation efforts. A Force Majeure Event shall not excuse the affected Party\'s obligation to make any payment that was due and owing prior to the occurrence of such Force Majeure Event.

**Section 12.2** *Allocation During Force Majeure.* During any period in which performance of any Service is affected by a Force Majeure Event, the Fees for the affected Service shall be equitably adjusted to reflect the actual level of Services delivered during such period.     tcPr=cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd=tcPr.find(qn('w:shd'))

        shd=OxmlElement('w:shd'); tcPr.append(shd)
    shd.set(qn('w:fill'), fill)

def set_cell_text_markup(cell, old, new):
    p=cell.paragraphs[0]
    for child in list(p._p):

No consent or approval of Service Recipient shall be required, and no employee shall be deemed dedicated to Service Recipient.'
set_markup(p43,'Section 4.3 Key Personnel.',old43.split('. ',1)[1],new43.split('. ',1)[1])
add_comment(doc,p43,'C-02','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §7.1 and §7.1 Key Negotiation Points.','The buyer consent right over reassignment, termination, and replacement of named employees could lock Polaris personnel into the divested business, create employment-law complications, and impair resource allocation across four divisions.','Firm on no consent requirement and sole staffing discretion. Advance notice and a qualified replacement commitment are reasonable negotiation accommodations.')

p52=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 5.2 Automatic Renewal.')
old52=p52.text
new52='Section 5.2 Extensions. This Agreement shall expire at the end of the Initial Term and shall not renew automatically. The Parties may extend the term for an individual Service only by a written amendment signed by both Parties before expiration of the applicable Service, for a period not exceeding six (6) months beyond the Initial Term. Any extension shall be priced at cost plus fifteen percent (15%) and shall otherwise be on terms mutually agreed in writing. No extension shall be effective by silence, course of dealing, or failure to deliver a notice of non-renewal.'
set_markup(p52,'Section 5.2 Extensions.',old52.split('. ',1)[1],new52.split('. ',1)[1])
add_comment(doc,p52,'C-03','CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','APA §7.12(a); Playbook §3.1.','Automatic renewal can extend the TSA beyond the APA hard stop, leaves Polaris with an open-ended service obligation unless it tracks a 120-day notice deadline, and eliminates extension-price leverage.','Firm: delete automatic renewal. Any extension must be mutual, written, and capped at six months; target extension pricing is cost-plus-15%.')

p53=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 5.3 Termination of Individual Services.')
old53=p53.text
new53='Section 5.3 Termination of Individual Services. Either Party may terminate any individual Service upon not less than ninety (90) days\' prior written notice to the other Party, specifying in reasonable detail the Service to be terminated and the effective date. Termination of an individual Service shall not affect any other Service. Service Recipient shall pay all Fees accrued through the effective date and reimburse any non-cancelable costs or commitments incurred by Service Provider in reasonable reliance on continuation of the Service, subject to Service Provider\'s commercially reasonable mitigation efforts.'
set_markup(p53,'Section 5.3 Termination of Individual Services.',old53.split('. ',1)[1],new53.split('. ',1)[1])
add_comment(doc,p53,'C-04','CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','APA §7.12(c) expressly makes 90 days the minimum and maximum notice period.','The draft’s 120-day period is a direct APA conflict and locks Polaris into service obligations for an extra month after notice.','Firm APA-compliance position; retain the non-cancelable-cost protection included in the proposed language.')

p54=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 5.4 Termination for Cause.')
old54=p54.text
new54='Section 5.4 Termination for Cause. Either Party may terminate this Agreement in whole, or with respect to any individual Service, upon written notice if the other Party materially breaches this Agreement and fails to cure within thirty (30) days after notice. Service Provider may terminate immediately upon written notice, without a cure period, if Service Recipient (a) becomes insolvent or commences or has commenced against it a bankruptcy or similar proceeding, (b) fails to pay an undisputed invoice more than sixty (60) days after its due date, or (c) engages in conduct that creates material legal, regulatory, or reputational risk for Service Provider. The foregoing rights are in addition to any other rights expressly stated in this Agreement.'
set_markup(p54,'Section 5.4 Termination for Cause.',old54.split('. ',1)[1],new54.split('. ',1)[1])
add_comment(doc,p54,'C-05','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §3.3.','Without immediate termination rights for insolvency or prolonged non-payment, Polaris may be required to continue funding services for a distressed buyer; reputational or regulatory exposure may also make continued performance untenable.','Firm on insolvency and non-payment. The reputational-risk trigger is a strong seller position but can be narrowed to material, reasonably documented risk if needed.')

p57=find_para_contains(doc,'(d) all rights and obligations of the Parties with respect to the terminated or expired Services')
add_insert_after(doc,p57,'Section 5.5(e) Termination Assistance.', 'At Service Recipient\'s written request made before the effective date of termination, Service Provider shall provide reasonable termination assistance for a period not to exceed sixty (60) days, solely to support knowledge transfer, data migration, transition documentation, and cooperation with a replacement provider. Termination assistance shall be provided at Service Provider\'s Fully-Loaded Cost plus fifteen percent (15%), shall be subject to a mutually agreed written work plan, and shall not be required while Service Recipient has any undisputed unpaid amount or if the requested assistance would require Service Provider to retain personnel, acquire resources, or breach law or a third-party obligation.', ('C-06','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §3.4.','The draft is silent on wind-down boundaries, creating an argument for open-ended post-termination cooperation and uncompensated transition work.','Firm on a defined, compensated period and no assistance while undisputed invoices remain unpaid. Period and markup may move to 90 days / cost-plus-10% as fallback.'))

p61=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 6.1 Service Charges.')
old61=p61.text
new61='Section 6.1 Service Charges. Fees shall be calculated for each Service category on the basis of the actual Fully-Loaded Cost incurred by Service Provider in providing that category, plus a uniform markup of ten percent (10%) of such Fully-Loaded Cost, subject to the estimates, five-percent (5%) consent threshold, and other requirements of APA §7.12(b). The Fee Schedule sets forth estimated costs and fees for convenience and shall not be construed to waive Service Provider\'s right to invoice actual Fully-Loaded Costs in accordance with the APA and this Agreement. No additional charge shall be imposed except as expressly permitted by a signed change order or as reimbursable under this Agreement.'
set_markup(p61,'Section 6.1 Service Charges.',old61.split('. ',1)[1],new61.split('. ',1)[1])
add_comment(doc,p61,'C-07','CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','APA §7.12(b) requires cost-plus pricing based on actual Fully-Loaded Cost, a markup not exceeding 10%, and adjustment mechanics subject to the five-percent estimate threshold.','The draft’s fixed-fee framing and the 15% IT line are inconsistent with the APA and could either undercompensate Polaris for actual costs or create a credibility problem if Trident challenges the fee schedule.','Firm on APA mechanics and uniform 10% ceiling. Annual escalation and change-order economics remain negotiation positions, subject to APA limits.')

p63=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 6.3 Payment.')
old63=p63.text
new63='Section 6.3 Payment. Service Recipient shall pay each undisputed invoice within thirty (30) days after the date of invoice. Any undisputed portion shall be paid when due notwithstanding a dispute regarding another portion. Late amounts shall accrue interest at the lesser of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month or the maximum rate permitted by Applicable Law.'
set_markup(p63,'Section 6.3 Payment.',old63.split('. ',1)[1],new63.split('. ',1)[1])
add_comment(doc,p63,'C-08','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §4.3.','“Commercially reasonable time” is vague and weakens Polaris’s cash-flow protection; the draft also lacks late interest.','Target Net 30 / 1.5% per month. Net 45 and 1.0% per month are the playbook fallback positions.')

p64=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 6.4 Fee Escalation.')
old64=p64.text
new64='Section 6.4 Fee Escalation and Cost Changes. Subject to APA §7.12(b), on each anniversary of the Closing Date the estimated Fees shall be adjusted by the greater of (a) three percent (3%) or (b) the increase in CPI-U over the preceding twelve (12) months. In addition, Service Provider may propose an equitable adjustment for an Escalation Event, including a material increase in costs resulting from a change in law or regulation, vendor pricing, or a material increase in volume or scope requested by Service Recipient. Any adjustment remains subject to the APA\'s actual Fully-Loaded Cost and five-percent (5%) consent limitations.'
set_markup(p64,'Section 6.4 Fee Escalation and Cost Changes.',old64.split('. ',1)[1],new64.split('. ',1)[1])
add_comment(doc,p64,'SIGNIFICANT','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §4.2; APA §7.12(b) preserved by express savings language.','Fixed fees without a cost-change mechanism create a below-market incentive for Trident to delay migration and leave Polaris carrying inflation, regulatory, and vendor-cost risk.','Target greater of 3% or CPI-U plus Escalation Event; CPI-U only is the fallback. Any increase that implicates the APA five-percent threshold requires Buyer consent.')

p66=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 6.6 Disputed Amounts.')
add_insert_after(doc,p66,'Section 6.7 Change Orders.', 'Any request for services not expressly described in a Schedule, a material increase in volume, or a material change in scope shall be effective only through a written change order signed by authorized representatives of both Parties. Service Provider may accept or reject a requested change in its sole discretion. A change order shall specify scope, timing, assumptions, and pricing, which shall be cost plus fifteen percent (15%) unless otherwise agreed in writing; no work shall begin until the change order is fully executed and any agreed advance payment is received. Informal requests, course of dealing, or Service Recipient instructions shall not expand the Services or Fees.', ('C-09','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §4.4.','Without a written change-order gate, Trident can expand scope informally and later contend the expanded work is included in the existing fee.','Firm on written dual signature and no obligation before execution. Cost-plus-10% is the fallback if Trident pushes back on the target markup.'))

p71=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 7.1 Service Provider Materials')
old71=p71.text
new71='Section 7.1 Service Provider Materials — Ownership; No License. Service Provider and its Affiliates retain all right, title, and interest in and to all Service Provider Materials, including tools, methodologies, templates, processes, software, systems, know-how, and processes, whether existing before or developed during the Term. No license, sublicense, right to use, right to copy, right to modify, right to create derivative works, or other interest in any Service Provider Materials is granted to Service Recipient by this Agreement, whether expressly, by implication, estoppel, or otherwise. Service Recipient may access and use Service Provider Materials only to the limited extent necessary to receive the Services during the applicable Service Period, and all such access shall cease upon expiration or termination. Any post-termination use requested by Service Recipient must be addressed in a separate written license agreement with separate consideration and appropriate restrictions.'
set_markup(p71,'Section 7.1 Service Provider Materials — Ownership; No License.',old71.split('. ',1)[1],new71.split('. ',1)[1])
add_comment(doc,p71,'CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','Andersen instructions; Playbook §6.1.','The draft grants a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free, sublicensable license to operational IP used across Polaris’s divisions, risking IP leakage and competitive harm.','Firm, board-level position: delete the license entirely. Any post-TSA tool access must be handled under a separate negotiated license with compensation and restrictions.')

p72=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 7.2 Service Recipient Materials.')
old72=p72.text
new72='Section 7.2 Data Ownership and Return. Service Recipient retains ownership of data relating exclusively to the Business that is provided to or generated for Service Recipient after Closing (Buyer Data). Service Provider retains ownership of all Service Provider systems, infrastructure, tools, methodologies, security data, system-level data, pre-Closing data, and data relating to Polaris or its other businesses. Service Provider shall use Buyer Data only to perform the Services and shall reasonably cooperate in exporting Buyer Data in a commonly used machine-readable format at the end of the applicable Service Period, subject to payment of accrued Fees and reasonable transition charges. Neither Party is required to disclose or transfer the other Party\'s proprietary information or any data that cannot lawfully be transferred.'
set_markup(p72,'Section 7.2 Data Ownership and Return.',old72.split('. ',1)[1],new72.split('. ',1)[1])
add_comment(doc,p72,'SIGNIFICANT','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §6.2.','The draft treats all Trident-provided materials alike and does not reserve Polaris’s systems, pre-Closing data, system-level metadata, or proprietary information, potentially turning routine migration into a broader data-transfer obligation.','Accept reasonable Buyer Data migration, but preserve Polaris ownership and confidentiality of systems, pre-Closing data, and other-division data.')

p78=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 8.4 Data Privacy.')
old78=p78.text
new78='Section 8.4 Data Privacy. Each Party shall comply with all applicable data privacy and data protection laws in connection with its performance under this Agreement, including U.S. laws and, to the extent applicable to processing involving individuals in Mexico, Mexico\'s Federal Law on Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties (Ley Federal de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de los Particulares, or LFPDPPP) and its Regulations. Each Party shall implement and maintain appropriate technical and organizational measures to protect personal data against unauthorized access, use, disclosure, alteration, or destruction.'
set_markup(p78,'Section 8.4 Data Privacy.',old78.split('. ',1)[1],new78.split('. ',1)[1])
add_comment(doc,p78,'CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','APA §7.12(g); Playbook §6.3; Andersen instructions.','The draft references only U.S. privacy law even though Polaris will process personal data for 300+ Mexican employees; this creates LFPDPPP compliance, consent, transfer, and enforcement risk.','Firm that the TSA must expressly cover LFPDPPP. The detailed allocation below is substantive and should be validated by Mexico/LatAm counsel before execution.')
add_insert_after(doc,p78,'Section 8.5 Mexico Data Processing Terms.', 'For Monterrey employee and other Mexico personal data: (a) Service Recipient is the data controller/responsible party and shall provide or cause to be provided compliant privacy notices (avisos de privacidad), obtain any required consents and authorizations for processing and cross-border transfers, and provide accurate, lawful instructions; (b) Service Provider is a processor/service provider and shall process such data only on documented instructions and only to perform the Services; (c) Service Provider shall maintain appropriate administrative, technical, and physical safeguards, restrict access to personnel with a need to know, and require equivalent obligations of Affiliates and subcontractors; (d) Service Provider shall notify Service Recipient without undue delay and, in any event, within seventy-two (72) hours after becoming aware of a security incident involving such data, and shall reasonably cooperate in investigation, mitigation, notices, and regulatory responses; (e) each Party shall assist the other with data-subject requests, audits, and legally required notices to the extent relevant to its role; and (f) upon expiration or termination, Service Provider shall return or securely delete such data at Service Recipient\'s direction, except to the extent retention is required by law, in which case it remains protected under this Article 8. The Parties shall execute any supplemental data-processing addendum reasonably required to document these terms.', ('C-10','CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','APA §7.12(g); Playbook §6.3; client instructions.','Without controller/processor allocation, privacy notices, cross-border transfer mechanics, safeguards, and breach cooperation, Polaris could be exposed to enforcement, employee claims, and operational disruption in Mexico.','Firm on allocation and core safeguards. Exact consent mechanics and addendum form should be confirmed by Mexico counsel; this is not intended to shift Buyer’s controller responsibilities to Polaris.'))

# indemnity
p82=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 9.1 Service Recipient Indemnification.')
old82=p82.text
new82='Section 9.1 Service Recipient Indemnification. Service Recipient shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Service Provider and its Affiliates and their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, successors, and assigns from and against Losses arising from third-party claims to the extent resulting from Service Recipient\'s use of or reliance on the Services, Service Recipient\'s breach of this Agreement, or the negligent or wrongful act or omission of Service Recipient or its personnel in connection with this Agreement, except to the extent the third-party claim results from Service Provider\'s gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct. The indemnity in this Section is subject to Section 10.1.'
set_markup(p82,'Section 9.1 Service Recipient Indemnification.',old82.split('. ',1)[1],new82.split('. ',1)[1])
add_comment(doc,p82,'SIGNIFICANT','SIGNIFICANT','APA §7.12(d); Playbook §5.3.','The draft covers direct first-party losses and broad breach/law theories, which can bypass the APA’s contemplated third-party indemnity structure and create uncapped exposure through carve-out arguments.','Firm on third-party-only scope and cap application; proportionate-fault wording may be a fallback.')
p83=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 9.2 Service Provider Indemnification.')
old83=p83.text
new83='Section 9.2 Service Provider Indemnification. Service Provider shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Service Recipient and its Affiliates and their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, successors, and assigns solely from and against Losses arising from third-party claims, but only to the extent such claims result from Service Provider\'s gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct in performing the Services. The indemnity in this Section is subject to Section 10.1 and does not create liability for ordinary negligence, a breach of this Agreement, or a violation of law unrelated to gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct.'
set_markup(p83,'Section 9.2 Service Provider Indemnification.',old83.split('. ',1)[1],new83.split('. ',1)[1])
add_comment(doc,p83,'CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','APA §7.12(d)(iii); Playbook §5.3.','The draft makes Polaris indemnify for any breach of covenant, representation, or law violation and does not limit the obligation to third-party claims, expanding the APA carve-out and threatening the agreed liability allocation.','Firm APA-compliance position: third-party claims only and gross negligence/fraud/willful misconduct threshold.')

p89=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 10.1 Aggregate Liability Cap.')
old89=p89.text
new89='Section 10.1 Aggregate Liability Cap. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, the aggregate liability of Service Provider and its Affiliates, and their respective officers, directors, employees, and agents, arising out of or related to this Agreement shall not exceed the total TSA Fees actually paid by Service Recipient to Service Provider during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the date on which the applicable claim is first asserted in writing by Service Recipient. During the first twelve (12) months after the Closing Date, the cap shall equal the TSA Fees actually paid from the Closing Date through the date the claim is first asserted in writing. The cap applies in the aggregate and not per claim. The limitation shall not apply to (i) a Party\'s fraud or willful misconduct, (ii) a Party\'s breach of its confidentiality obligations, or (iii) Service Provider\'s indemnification obligations for third-party claims, but only to the extent such claims result from Service Provider\'s gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct. This Section is intended to implement APA §7.12(d) and shall be construed accordingly.'
set_markup(p89,'Section 10.1 Aggregate Liability Cap.',old89.split('. ',1)[1],new89.split('. ',1)[1])
add_comment(doc,p89,'CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','APA §7.12(d); Andersen instructions; Playbook §5.1.','The draft uses 200% of all fees paid, creating a materially higher cap than the APA-required rolling 12-month fee cap and does not expressly cover Polaris Affiliates and personnel.','Firm, non-negotiable APA conflict. Illustrative exposure: draft at $1.139M/month for 18 months = $20.502M fees; 200% cap = $41.004M. APA cap after 12 months = $13.464M at corrected $1.122M/month; delta = $27.540M, or approximately 3.05x.')

p90=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 10.2 Consequential Damages.')
old90=p90.text
new90='Section 10.2 Consequential Damages. EACH PARTY HEREBY WAIVES, AND SHALL NOT ASSERT AGAINST THE OTHER PARTY, ANY AND ALL CLAIMS FOR CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, PUNITIVE, EXEMPLARY, OR INDIRECT DAMAGES, INCLUDING LOSS OF REVENUE, LOSS OF PROFITS, LOSS OF BUSINESS OPPORTUNITY, COST OF REPLACEMENT SERVICES, DIMINUTION OF VALUE, OR LOSS OF GOODWILL, ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT, REGARDLESS OF THEORY OR WHETHER ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY. This mutual waiver shall not limit liability for fraud or willful misconduct, breach of confidentiality, infringement or misappropriation of intellectual property, or third-party claims for which indemnification is available under Article 9, and shall apply notwithstanding failure of essential purpose of any remedy.'
set_markup(p90,'Section 10.2 Consequential Damages.',old90.split('. ',1)[1],new90.split('. ',1)[1])
add_comment(doc,p90,'CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','APA §7.12(d) requires a mutual waiver; Playbook §5.2; Andersen instructions.','The draft is one-way: Polaris waives claims against Trident but Trident does not waive consequential-damage claims against Polaris, leaving Polaris exposed to business-interruption and replacement-service damages.','Firm on mutuality. Narrow carve-outs for confidentiality, IP, and indemnified third-party claims are consistent with the playbook; fraud/willful misconduct may be retained.')

p97=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 12.1 Force Majeure.')
old97=p97.text
new97='Section 12.1 Force Majeure. Neither Party shall be liable for failure or delay caused by a Force Majeure Event beyond its reasonable control, including natural disasters, pandemics, war or terrorism, government action, sanctions or embargoes, strikes, power or telecommunications failures, internet outages, or cyberattacks. The affected Party shall promptly notify the other, use commercially reasonable mitigation efforts, and keep the other reasonably informed. Obligations are suspended, not terminated, during the event, and payment obligations accrued before the event remain due. If the Force Majeure Event continues for ninety (90) consecutive days and materially prevents performance of an affected Service, either Party may terminate that affected Service on written notice without penalty, subject to payment of accrued Fees and any agreed termination assistance.'
set_markup(p97,'Section 12.1 Force Majeure.',old97.split('. ',1)[1],new97.split('. ',1)[1])
add_comment(doc,p97,'SIGNIFICANT','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §10.1.','The draft excuses delay indefinitely but provides no exit if a prolonged outage makes continued performance impracticable or leaves Polaris bearing resource and reputational risk.','Target 90-day trigger; 120 days is the maximum fallback.')

p101=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 13.1 Service Recipient Insurance.')
old101=p101.text
new101='Section 13.1 Service Recipient Insurance. Service Recipient shall maintain during the Term and for twelve (12) months thereafter: (a) commercial general liability insurance of at least $5,000,000 per occurrence and $5,000,000 aggregate; (b) umbrella or excess liability insurance of at least $5,000,000; and (c) workers\' compensation insurance at statutory limits. Polaris and its Affiliates shall be named as additional insureds under the CGL and umbrella/excess policies, which shall include a waiver of subrogation in favor of Polaris and its Affiliates. Policies shall be issued by insurers rated at least A- by A.M. Best. Service Recipient shall deliver certificates and applicable endorsements within ten (10) Business Days after Closing and annually thereafter.'
set_markup(p101,'Section 13.1 Service Recipient Insurance.',old101.split('. ',1)[1],new101.split('. ',1)[1])
add_comment(doc,p101,'SIGNIFICANT','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §8.1.','The draft provides only $2M CGL and omits umbrella coverage, additional-insured protection, waiver of subrogation, workers’ compensation, and delivery timing, leaving Polaris exposed to industrial-operations claims.','Target $5M CGL + $5M umbrella and endorsements. $3M limits are the absolute fallback; do not waive umbrella or additional-insured status.')

p103=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 14.1 Audit Rights.')
old103=p103.text
new103='Section 14.1 Audit Rights. Service Recipient may, at its sole expense and no more than once in any twelve (12)-month period, audit Service Provider\'s books and records solely to verify Fees, upon at least thirty (30) Business Days\' prior written notice. Any audit shall occur during normal business hours, in a manner that does not unreasonably interfere with operations, and shall be conducted by Service Recipient or one independent auditor bound by confidentiality obligations reasonably satisfactory to Service Provider. The audit shall be limited to fee-related records for the audited period and shall exclude proprietary systems, internal cost methodologies, unrelated personnel records, privileged material, and information concerning other Polaris businesses. Service Recipient shall keep audit results confidential and shall not disclose them except to its Representatives with a need to know or as required by law.'
set_markup(p103,'Section 14.1 Audit Rights.',old103.split('. ',1)[1],new103.split('. ',1)[1])
add_comment(doc,p103,'SIGNIFICANT','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §9.1.','Two audits per calendar year at Polaris’s expense, with 10 business days’ notice and access to systems/personnel, is disruptive and invites fishing expeditions into proprietary information.','Target once per 12 months, 30 days, buyer expense, fee records only. Twice per TSA term / 20 days is the fallback.')
p104=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 14.2 Audit Adjustments.')
old104=p104.text
new104='Section 14.2 Audit Adjustments. If an audit shows an overcharge for the audited period exceeding five percent (5%), Service Provider shall credit the overcharge within thirty (30) days after written demand and reimburse Service Recipient\'s reasonable, documented audit costs. If the overcharge is five percent (5%) or less, Service Provider shall credit the overcharge but shall not be responsible for audit costs. If an audit shows an undercharge, Service Recipient shall pay the deficiency within thirty (30) days after Service Provider\'s written demand. Any interest shall be at the lesser of one percent (1%) per month or the maximum lawful rate.'
set_markup(p104,'Section 14.2 Audit Adjustments.',old104.split('. ',1)[1],new104.split('. ',1)[1])
add_comment(doc,p104,'SIGNIFICANT','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §9.1.','The draft makes Polaris pay audit interest and costs without a materiality threshold, incentivizing frequent or low-value audits.','Retain credit for any verified overcharge; reimburse audit costs only where the overcharge exceeds 5%.')

p105=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 15.1 Governing Law.')
old105=p105.text
new105='Section 15.1 Governing Law. This Agreement and all claims arising out of or relating to it shall be governed by the internal laws of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, without regard to conflict-of-laws principles that would require application of another jurisdiction\'s law.'
set_markup(p105,'Section 15.1 Governing Law.',old105.split('. ',1)[1],new105.split('. ',1)[1])
add_comment(doc,p105,'SIGNIFICANT','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §11.1; APA §12.3 permits the TSA to specify its governing law.','Ohio law gives Trident a home-state advantage despite Polaris’s Pennsylvania headquarters, personnel base, and counsel.','Target Pennsylvania law. Delaware is the fallback if required to match the APA; do not accept Ohio as the default.')
p106=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 15.2 Dispute Resolution.')
old106=p106.text
new106='Section 15.2 Dispute Resolution. Any dispute shall first be escalated to the Parties\' designated CFO- or General Counsel-level representatives, who shall have fifteen (15) Business Days to resolve it. Either Party may then request non-binding mediation. If unresolved, the dispute shall be finally resolved by confidential binding arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association under its Commercial Arbitration Rules, before one arbitrator with relevant industry experience, seated in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Judgment on the award may be entered in any court of competent jurisdiction. This Section does not limit either Party\'s right to seek temporary or injunctive relief to protect Confidential Information or intellectual property.'
set_markup(p106,'Section 15.2 Dispute Resolution.',old106.split('. ',1)[1],new106.split('. ',1)[1])
add_comment(doc,p106,'SIGNIFICANT','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §11.2.','Cuyahoga County litigation exposes Polaris to buyer-home-jurisdiction procedure, public dockets, broad discovery, and jury-waiver enforcement risk.','Target executive escalation, optional mediation, and AAA arbitration in Pittsburgh. Neutral venue or a three-arbitrator panel for disputes over $5M are negotiation fallbacks.')

p109=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 15.5 Entire Agreement.')
old109=p109.text
new109='Section 15.5 Entire Agreement; APA Precedence. This Agreement, its Schedules, the Purchase Agreement, and the other Transaction Documents constitute the entire agreement regarding their subject matter. In the event of conflict between this Agreement and the Purchase Agreement, the Purchase Agreement shall control unless this Agreement expressly states, with specific reference to the applicable provision of the Purchase Agreement, that the Parties intend to supersede that provision and each Party executes this Agreement with actual knowledge of the conflict. A general integration clause or general statement that this Agreement controls shall not supersede any APA provision. For the avoidance of doubt, the terms of APA §7.12 control where they impose a mandatory requirement on this Agreement.'
set_markup(p109,'Section 15.5 Entire Agreement; APA Precedence.',old109.split('. ',1)[1],new109.split('. ',1)[1])
add_comment(doc,p109,'CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','APA §12.5 requires APA supremacy absent a specific, express supersession reference and actual knowledge.','The draft’s broad exception could allow the TSA to override the APA without identifying the specific APA provision, undermining the binding 7.12 constraints and creating closing/post-closing dispute risk.','Firm: preserve APA supremacy and specific-reference requirement.')

p112=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 15.11 Interpretation.')

def add_insert_after(doc, anchor, heading, text, comment=None):
    p=doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(4)
    r=p.add_run('[ADDED] '+heading+' '); r.bold=True; r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(0x00,0x55,0xAA); r.font.underline=True; r.font.size=Pt(9)
    r=p.add_run(text); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(0x00,0x55,0xAA); r.font.underline=True; r.font.size=Pt(8.5)
    anchor._p.addnext(p._p)
    if comment:
        add_comment(doc,p,*comment)
    return p

def find_para(doc, starts):
    if isinstance(starts,str): starts=[starts]
    for p in doc.paragraphs:
        if any(p.text.startswith(s) for s in starts): return p
    raise KeyError(starts)

def find_para_contains(doc, token):
    for p in doc.paragraphs:
        if token in p.text: return p
    raise KeyError(token)

def prepend_paragraph(doc, text, size=9, bold=False, color=None, align=None):
    p=doc.add_paragraph()
    r=p.add_run(text); r.font.size=Pt(size); r.bold=bold
    if color: r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(*color)
    if align: p.alignment=align
    first=doc._body._body[0]
    first.addprevious(p._p)
    return p

def mpara(text='', bold=False, color=None, size=9.5, align=None, before=0, after=4):
    p=md.add_paragraph(); p.paragraph_format.space_before=Pt(before); p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(after)

    r=p.add_run(text); r.bold=bold; r.font.size=Pt(size)

def memo_table(headers, rows, widths=None):
    t=md.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(headers)); t.style='Table Grid'; t.alignment=WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    for i,h in enumerate(headers):
        c=t.rows[0].cells[i]; c.text=h; set_cell_shading(c,'D9EAF7')
        for r in c.paragraphs[0].runs: r.bold=True; r.font.size=Pt(8.5); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(31,78,121)
    for row in rows:
        cells=t.add_row().cells
        for i,val in enumerate(row):
            cells[i].text=str(val)
            for p in cells[i].paragraphs:
                for r in p.runs: r.font.size=Pt(8.2)
    for row in t.rows:
        for c in row.cells: c.vertical_alignment=WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT.TOP
    return t

{"command":"cat > build_deliverables.py <<'PY'
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Inches, Pt, RGBColor
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.enum.section import WD_SECTION
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT, WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT
from docx.enum.style import WD_STYLE_TYPE
from copy import deepcopy
import os, re, math

SRC='documents/trident-draft-tsa.docx'
OUT='output'
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)

# ---------- Shared helpers ----------
def set_cell_shading(cell, fill):
    tcPr=cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd=tcPr.find(qn('w:shd'))
    if shd is None:
        shd=OxmlElement('w:shd'); tcPr.append(shd)
    shd.set(qn('w:fill'), fill)

def set_cell_text_markup(cell, old, new):
    p=cell.paragraphs[0]
    for child in list(p._p):
        if child.tag != qn('w:pPr'):
            p._p.remove(child)
    r=p.add_run('[DEL] '+old)
    r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(0xC0,0x00,0x00); r.font.strike=True; r.font.size=Pt(8)
    r=p.add_run('  [ADD] '+new)
    r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(0x00,0x55,0xAA); r.font.underline=True; r.font.size=Pt(8)
    set_cell_shading(cell,'FFF0F0')

def clear_paragraph(p):
    for child in list(p._p):
        if child.tag != qn('w:pPr'):
            p._p.remove(child)

def set_markup(p, lead, deleted, added):
    clear_paragraph(p)
    r=p.add_run(lead)
    r.bold=True
    r.font.size=Pt(9)
    r=p.add_run('\n[DELETED] '+deleted)
    r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(0xC0,0x00,0x00); r.font.strike=True; r.font.size=Pt(8.5)
    r=p.add_run('\n[ADDED] '+added)
    r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(0x00,0x55,0xAA); r.font.underline=True; r.font.size=Pt(8.5)
    p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(4)

def set_added(p, lead, added):
    clear_paragraph(p)
    r=p.add_run(lead); r.bold=True; r.font.size=Pt(9)
    r=p.add_run('\n[ADDED] '+added); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(0x00,0x55,0xAA); r.font.underline=True; r.font.size=Pt(8.5)

def add_comment(doc, anchor, code, priority, basis, risk, posture):
    cp=doc.add_paragraph()
    cp.style='Normal'
    cp.paragraph_format.left_indent=Inches(0.18)
    cp.paragraph_format.right_indent=Inches(0.08)
    cp.paragraph_format.space_before=Pt(2); cp.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(5)
    cp.paragraph_format.keep_together=True
    pPr=cp._p.get_or_add_pPr()
    shd=OxmlElement('w:shd'); shd.set(qn('w:fill'), 'EAF2F8'); pPr.append(shd)
    bord=OxmlElement('w:pBdr')
    for side in ['left']:
        el=OxmlElement('w:'+side); el.set(qn('w:val'),'single'); el.set(qn('w:sz'),'18'); el.set(qn('w:space'),'6'); el.set(qn('w:color'),'5B9BD5'); bord.append(el)
    pPr.append(bord)
    r=cp.add_run(f'COMMENT {code}  |  {priority}\n'); r.bold=True; r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(0x1F,0x4E,0x79); r.font.size=Pt(8.5)
    for label, text in [('Basis: ',basis),('Polaris risk: ',risk),('Position: ',posture)]:
        r=cp.add_run(label); r.bold=True; r.font.size=Pt(8.2); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(0x1F,0x1F,0x1F)
        r=cp.add_run(text+'\n'); r.font.size=Pt(8.2); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(0x1F,0x1F,0x1F)
    anchor._p.addnext(cp._p)
    return cp

def add_insert_after(doc, anchor, heading, text, comment=None):
    p=doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(4)
    r=p.add_run('[ADDED] '+heading+' '); r.bold=True; r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(0x00,0x55,0xAA); r.font.underline=True; r.font.size=Pt(9)
    r=p.add_run(text); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(0x00,0x55,0xAA); r.font.underline=True; r.font.size=Pt(8.5)
    anchor._p.addnext(p._p)
    if comment:
        add_comment(doc,p,*comment)
    return p

def find_para(doc, starts):
    if isinstance(starts,str): starts=[starts]
    for p in doc.paragraphs:
        if any(p.text.startswith(s) for s in starts): return p
    raise KeyError(starts)

def find_para_contains(doc, token):
    for p in doc.paragraphs:
        if token in p.text: return p
    raise KeyError(token)

def prepend_paragraph(doc, text, size=9, bold=False, color=None, align=None):
    p=doc.add_paragraph()
    r=p.add_run(text); r.font.size=Pt(size); r.bold=bold
    if color: r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(*color)
    if align: p.alignment=align
    first=doc._body._body[0]
    first.addprevious(p._p)
    return p

def add_page_break_before(p):
    p.paragraph_format.page_break_before=True

# ---------- Redline ----------
doc=Document(SRC)
# Page setup / styles
for sec in doc.sections:
    sec.top_margin=Inches(0.65); sec.bottom_margin=Inches(0.65); sec.left_margin=Inches(0.75); sec.right_margin=Inches(0.75)

# Cover sheet inserted ahead of draft
p=prepend_paragraph(doc,'SELLER-SIDE REDLINE — TRANSITION SERVICES AGREEMENT',15,True,(31,78,121),WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER)
p=prepend_paragraph(doc,'Polaris Industrial Holdings, Inc. / Trident Manufacturing Group, Inc.',10,False,(80,80,80),WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER)
p=prepend_paragraph(doc,'Prepared for Whitfield & Crane LLP | April 29, 2025 | Privileged & Confidential — Attorney-Client Work Product',8.5,False,(100,100,100),WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER)
p=prepend_paragraph(doc,'MARKUP CONVENTIONS',11,True,(31,78,121))
p=prepend_paragraph(doc,'[DELETED] Red strikethrough = seller deletion.  [ADDED] Blue underline = seller addition.  Shaded boxes = annotated comments identifying priority, basis, Polaris risk, and negotiation posture.',9,False)
p=prepend_paragraph(doc,'This markup is based on the executed APA excerpts (including Sections 7.12 and Exhibit H), the Polaris TSA Playbook (January 15, 2025), and Andersen instructions. It preserves the draft structure where practicable and flags conforming changes that should be made in the clean execution version.',8.5,False)
# keep first page visually separate
first_after=doc.paragraphs[0]
# modify key paragraphs
p31=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 3.1 Standard of Performance.')
old31=p31.text
new31='Section 3.1 Standard of Performance. Service Provider shall provide, or cause to be provided, each Service in a manner substantially consistent with the manner and quality at which such Service was provided to or on behalf of the Business during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the Closing Date. Historical practices, methodologies, systems, and resource levels during that period are the benchmark. Service Provider shall not be required to provide Services at a level exceeding that historical level, to prioritize Service Recipient over Service Provider\'s own businesses, or to adopt new methodologies, systems, standards, or best practices not in use for the Business during that period. Service Provider does not guarantee any particular outcome or result and shall allocate resources in a manner consistent with its historical practices, subject to the express terms of this Agreement.'
set_markup(p31,'Section 3.1 Standard of Performance.',old31.split('. ',1)[1],new31.split('. ',1)[1])
add_comment(doc,p31,'C-01','CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','APA §§7.12(a) and 7.12(f); Playbook §2.1.','The 24-month lookback, “equal to or better than,” and industry-best-practices overlay create a ratcheting standard that exceeds the APA benchmark and may require Polaris to over-resource the TSA or prioritize Trident over retained businesses.','Firm APA-compliance position. No best-practices overlay; no prioritization. “Commercially reasonable efforts” is the maximum fallback only if needed for deal resolution.')

p43=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 4.3 Key Personnel.')
old43=p43.text
new43='Section 4.3 Key Personnel. The individuals and allocations listed on Schedule H are provided for planning and continuity purposes only and do not create a minimum staffing commitment or restrict Service Provider\'s staffing decisions. Service Provider shall retain sole discretion to assign, reassign, promote, transfer, replace, or terminate any personnel providing Services, provided that Service Provider shall maintain reasonably qualified personnel sufficient to provide the Services in accordance with Section 3.1. Where practicable, Service Provider shall provide Service Recipient at least fifteen (15) Business Days\' advance written notice of a planned reassignment or replacement of a person identified on Schedule H and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to provide a reasonably qualified replacement. No consent or approval of Service Recipient shall be required, and no employee shall be deemed dedicated to Service Recipient.'
set_markup(p43,'Section 4.3 Key Personnel.',old43.split('. ',1)[1],new43.split('. ',1)[1])
add_comment(doc,p43,'C-02','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §7.1 and §7.1 Key Negotiation Points.','The buyer consent right over reassignment, termination, and replacement of named employees could lock Polaris personnel into the divested business, create employment-law complications, and impair resource allocation across four divisions.','Firm on no consent requirement and sole staffing discretion. Advance notice and a qualified replacement commitment are reasonable negotiation accommodations.')

p52=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 5.2 Automatic Renewal.')
old52=p52.text
new52='Section 5.2 Extensions. This Agreement shall expire at the end of the Initial Term and shall not renew automatically. The Parties may extend the term for an individual Service only by a written amendment signed by both Parties before expiration of the applicable Service, for a period not exceeding six (6) months beyond the Initial Term. Any extension shall be priced at cost plus fifteen percent (15%) and shall otherwise be on terms mutually agreed in writing. No extension shall be effective by silence, course of dealing, or failure to deliver a notice of non-renewal.'
set_markup(p52,'Section 5.2 Extensions.',old52.split('. ',1)[1],new52.split('. ',1)[1])
add_comment(doc,p52,'C-03','CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','APA §7.12(a); Playbook §3.1.','Automatic renewal can extend the TSA beyond the APA hard stop, leaves Polaris with an open-ended service obligation unless it tracks a 120-day notice deadline, and eliminates extension-price leverage.','Firm: delete automatic renewal. Any extension must be mutual, written, and capped at six months; target extension pricing is cost-plus-15%.')

p53=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 5.3 Termination of Individual Services.')
old53=p53.text
new53='Section 5.3 Termination of Individual Services. Either Party may terminate any individual Service upon not less than ninety (90) days\' prior written notice to the other Party, specifying in reasonable detail the Service to be terminated and the effective date. Termination of an individual Service shall not affect any other Service. Service Recipient shall pay all Fees accrued through the effective date and reimburse any non-cancelable costs or commitments incurred by Service Provider in reasonable reliance on continuation of the Service, subject to Service Provider\'s commercially reasonable mitigation efforts.'
set_markup(p53,'Section 5.3 Termination of Individual Services.',old53.split('. ',1)[1],new53.split('. ',1)[1])
add_comment(doc,p53,'C-04','CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','APA §7.12(c) expressly makes 90 days the minimum and maximum notice period.','The draft’s 120-day period is a direct APA conflict and locks Polaris into service obligations for an extra month after notice.','Firm APA-compliance position; retain the non-cancelable-cost protection included in the proposed language.')

p54=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 5.4 Termination for Cause.')
old54=p54.text
new54='Section 5.4 Termination for Cause. Either Party may terminate this Agreement in whole, or with respect to any individual Service, upon written notice if the other Party materially breaches this Agreement and fails to cure within thirty (30) days after notice. Service Provider may terminate immediately upon written notice, without a cure period, if Service Recipient (a) becomes insolvent or commences or has commenced against it a bankruptcy or similar proceeding, (b) fails to pay an undisputed invoice more than sixty (60) days after its due date, or (c) engages in conduct that creates material legal, regulatory, or reputational risk for Service Provider. The foregoing rights are in addition to any other rights expressly stated in this Agreement.'
set_markup(p54,'Section 5.4 Termination for Cause.',old54.split('. ',1)[1],new54.split('. ',1)[1])
add_comment(doc,p54,'C-05','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §3.3.','Without immediate termination rights for insolvency or prolonged non-payment, Polaris may be required to continue funding services for a distressed buyer; reputational or regulatory exposure may also make continued performance untenable.','Firm on insolvency and non-payment. The reputational-risk trigger is a strong seller position but can be narrowed to material, reasonably documented risk if needed.')

p57=find_para_contains(doc,'(d) all rights and obligations of the Parties with respect to the terminated or expired Services')
add_insert_after(doc,p57,'Section 5.5(e) Termination Assistance.', 'At Service Recipient\'s written request made before the effective date of termination, Service Provider shall provide reasonable termination assistance for a period not to exceed sixty (60) days, solely to support knowledge transfer, data migration, transition documentation, and cooperation with a replacement provider. Termination assistance shall be provided at Service Provider\'s Fully-Loaded Cost plus fifteen percent (15%), shall be subject to a mutually agreed written work plan, and shall not be required while Service Recipient has any undisputed unpaid amount or if the requested assistance would require Service Provider to retain personnel, acquire resources, or breach law or a third-party obligation.', ('C-06','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §3.4.','The draft is silent on wind-down boundaries, creating an argument for open-ended post-termination cooperation and uncompensated transition work.','Firm on a defined, compensated period and no assistance while undisputed invoices remain unpaid. Period and markup may move to 90 days / cost-plus-10% as fallback.'))

# remove renewal definition and update Term definition
pdef=find_para_contains(doc,'"Renewal Term" means')
set_markup(pdef,'"Renewal Term" definition.',pdef.text,'[DELETED IN FULL — no automatic-renewal concept retained.]')
pterm=find_para_contains(doc,'"Term" means')
oldterm=pterm.text
newterm='"Term" means the Initial Term, together with any individual-Service extension expressly documented in a written amendment signed by both Parties under Section 5.2.'
set_markup(pterm,'"Term" definition.',oldterm,newterm)

p61=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 6.1 Service Charges.')
old61=p61.text
new61='Section 6.1 Service Charges. Fees shall be calculated for each Service category on the basis of the actual Fully-Loaded Cost incurred by Service Provider in providing that category, plus a uniform markup of ten percent (10%) of such Fully-Loaded Cost, subject to the estimates, five-percent (5%) consent threshold, and other requirements of APA §7.12(b). The Fee Schedule sets forth estimated costs and fees for convenience and shall not be construed to waive Service Provider\'s right to invoice actual Fully-Loaded Costs in accordance with the APA and this Agreement. No additional charge shall be imposed except as expressly permitted by a signed change order or as reimbursable under this Agreement.'
set_markup(p61,'Section 6.1 Service Charges.',old61.split('. ',1)[1],new61.split('. ',1)[1])
add_comment(doc,p61,'C-07','CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','APA §7.12(b) requires cost-plus pricing based on actual Fully-Loaded Cost, a markup not exceeding 10%, and adjustment mechanics subject to the five-percent estimate threshold.','The draft’s fixed-fee framing and the 15% IT line are inconsistent with the APA and could either undercompensate Polaris for actual costs or create a credibility problem if Trident challenges the fee schedule.','Firm on APA mechanics and uniform 10% ceiling. Annual escalation and change-order economics remain negotiation positions, subject to APA limits.')

p63=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 6.3 Payment.')
old63=p63.text
new63='Section 6.3 Payment. Service Recipient shall pay each undisputed invoice within thirty (30) days after the date of invoice. Late amounts shall accrue interest at the lesser of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month or the maximum rate permitted by Applicable Law.'
set_markup(p63,'Section 6.3 Payment.',old63.split('. ',1)[1],new63.split('. ',1)[1])
add_comment(doc,p63,'C-08','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §4.3.','“Commercially reasonable time” is vague and weakens Polaris’s cash-flow protection; the draft also lacks late interest.','Target Net 30 / 1.5% per month. Net 45 and 1.0% per month are the playbook fallback positions.')

p64=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 6.4 Fee Escalation.')

new64='Section 6.4 Fee Escalation and Cost Changes. p66=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 6.6 Disputed Amounts.')

p71=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 7.1 Service Provider Materials')
old71=p71.text
new71='Section 7.1 Service Provider Materials — Ownership; No License. old72=p72.text
new72='Section 7.2 Data Ownership and Return. p78=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 8.4 Data Privacy.')
old78=p78.text
new78='Section 8.4 Data Privacy. set_markup(p78,'Section 8.4 Data Privacy.',old78.split('. ',1)[1],new78.split('. ',1)[1])
add_comment(doc,p78,'CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','APA §7.12(g); Playbook §6.3; Andersen instructions.','The draft references only U.S. privacy law even though Polaris will process personal data for 300+ Mexican employees; this creates LFPDPPP compliance, consent, transfer, and enforcement risk.','Firm that the TSA must expressly cover LFPDPPP. The detailed allocation below is substantive and should be validated by Mexico/LatAm counsel before execution.')
add_insert_after(doc,p78,'Section 8.5 Mexico Data Processing Terms.', 'For Monterrey employee and other Mexico personal data: (a) Service Recipient is the data controller/responsible party and shall provide or cause to be provided compliant privacy notices (avisos de privacidad), obtain any required consents and authorizations for processing and cross-border transfers, and provide accurate, lawful instructions; (b) Service Provider is a processor/service provider and shall process such data only on documented instructions and only to perform the Services; (c) Service Provider shall maintain appropriate administrative, technical, and physical safeguards, restrict access to personnel with a need to know, and require equivalent obligations of Affiliates and subcontractors; (d) Service Provider shall notify Service Recipient without undue delay and, in any event, within seventy-two (72) hours after becoming aware of a security incident involving such data, and shall reasonably cooperate in investigation, mitigation, notices, and regulatory responses; (e) each Party shall assist the other with data-subject requests, audits, and legally required notices to the extent relevant to its role; and (f) upon expiration or termination, Service Provider shall return or securely delete such data at Service Recipient\'s direction, except to the extent retention is required by law, in which case it remains protected under this Article 8. The Parties shall execute any supplemental data-processing addendum reasonably required to document these terms.', ('C-10','CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','APA §7.12(g); Playbook §6.3; client instructions.','Without controller/processor allocation, privacy notices, cross-border transfer mechanics, safeguards, and breach cooperation, Polaris could be exposed to enforcement, employee claims, and operational disruption in Mexico.','Firm on allocation and core safeguards. Exact consent mechanics and addendum form should be confirmed by Mexico counsel; this is not intended to shift Buyer’s controller responsibilities to Polaris.'))

# indemnity
p82=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 9.1 Service Recipient Indemnification.')
old82=p82.text
new82='Section 9.1 Service Recipient Indemnification. Service Recipient shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Service Provider and its Affiliates and their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, successors, and assigns from and against Losses arising from third-party claims to the extent resulting from Service Recipient\'s use of or reliance on the Services, Service Recipient\'s breach of this Agreement, or the negligent or wrongful act or omission of Service Recipient or its personnel in connection with this Agreement, except to the extent the third-party claim results from Service Provider\'s gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct. set_markup(p82,'Section 9.1 Service Recipient Indemnification.',old82.split('. ',1)[1],new82.split('. ',1)[1])

p83=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 9.2 Service Provider Indemnification.')
old83=p83.text
new83='Section 9.2 Service Provider Indemnification.
