set_markup(p83,'Section 9.2 Service Provider Indemnification.',old83.split('. ',1)[1],new83.split('. ',1)[1])
add_comment(doc,p83,'CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','APA §7.12(d)(iii); Playbook §5.3.','The draft makes Polaris indemnify for any breach of covenant, representation, or law violation and does not limit the obligation to third-party claims, expanding the APA carve-out and threatening the agreed liability allocation.','Firm APA-compliance position: third-party claims only and gross negligence/fraud/willful misconduct threshold.')

p89=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 10.1 Aggregate Liability Cap.')
old89=p89.text
new89='Section 10.1 Aggregate Liability Cap. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, the aggregate liability of Service Provider and its Affiliates, and their respective officers, directors, employees, and agents, arising out of or related to this Agreement shall not exceed the total TSA Fees actually paid by Service Recipient to Service Provider during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the date on which the applicable claim is first asserted in writing by Service Recipient. During the first twelve (12) months after the Closing Date, the cap shall equal the TSA Fees actually paid from the Closing Date through the date the claim is first asserted in writing. The cap applies in the aggregate and not per claim. The limitation shall not apply to (i) a Party\'s fraud or willful misconduct, (ii) a Party\'s breach of its confidentiality obligations, or (iii) Service Provider\'s indemnification obligations for third-party claims, but only to the extent such claims result from Service Provider\'s gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct. Illustrative exposure: draft at $1.139M/month for 18 months = $20.502M fees; 200% cap = $41.004M. def mpara(text='', bold=False, color=None, size=9.5, align=None, before=0, after=4):
    p=md.add_paragraph(); p.paragraph_format.space_before=Pt(before); p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(after)
    if align: p.alignment=align
    r=p.add_run(text); r.bold=bold; r.font.size=Pt(size)
    if color: r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(*color)
    return p

def heading(text, level=1):
    p=md.add_paragraph(style=f'Heading {level}'); p.add_run(text); return p

def bullet(text, level=0):
    p=md.add_paragraph(style='List Bullet' if level==0 else 'List Bullet 2'); p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(2); p.add_run(text); return p

def memo_table(headers, rows, widths=None):
    t=md.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(headers)); t.style='Table Grid'; t.alignment=WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    for i,h in enumerate(headers):
        c=t.rows[0].cells[i]; c.text=h; set_cell_shading(c,'D9EAF7')
        for r in c.paragraphs[0].runs: r.bold=True; r.font.size=Pt(8.5); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(31,78,121)
    for row in rows:
        cells=t.add_row().cells
        for i,val in enumerate(row):
            cells[i].text=str(val)
            for p in cells[i].paragraphs:
                for r in p.runs: r.font.size=Pt(8.2)
    for row in t.rows:
        for c in row.cells: c.vertical_alignment=WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT.TOP
    return t

176: add_comment(doc,p63,'C-08','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §4.3.','“Commercially reasonable time” is vague and weakens Polaris’s cash-flow protection; the draft also lacks late interest.','Target Net 30 / 1.5% per month. Net 45 and 1.0% per month are the playbook fallback positions.')

178: p64=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 6.4 Fee Escalation.')
179: old64=p64.text
180: new64='Section 6.4 Fee Escalation and Cost Changes. Subject to APA §7.12(b), on each anniversary of the Closing Date the estimated Fees shall be adjusted by the greater of (a) three percent (3%) or (b) the increase in CPI-U over the preceding twelve (12) months. In addition, Service Provider may propose an equitable adjustment for an Escalation Event, including a material increase in costs resulting from a change in law or regulation, vendor pricing, or a material increase in volume or scope requested by Service Recipient. Any adjustment remains subject to the APA\'s actual Fully-Loaded Cost and five-percent (5%) consent limitations.'
181: set_markup(p64,'Section 6.4 Fee Escalation and Cost Changes.',old64.split('. ',1)[1],new64.split('. ',1)[1])
182: add_comment(doc,p64,'SIGNIFICANT','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §4.2; APA §7.12(b) preserved by express savings language.','Fixed fees without a cost-change mechanism create a below-market incentive for Trident to delay migration and leave Polaris carrying inflation, regulatory, and vendor-cost risk.','Target greater of 3% or CPI-U plus Escalation Event; CPI-U only is the fallback. Any increase that implicates the APA five-percent threshold requires Buyer consent.')

184: p66=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 6.6 Disputed Amounts.')
185: add_insert_after(doc,p66,'Section 6.7 Change Orders.', 'Any request for services not expressly described in a Schedule, a material increase in volume, or a material change in scope shall be effective only through a written change order signed by authorized representatives of both Parties. Service Provider may accept or reject a requested change in its sole discretion. A change order shall specify scope, timing, assumptions, and pricing, which shall be cost plus fifteen percent (15%) unless otherwise agreed in writing; no work shall begin until the change order is fully executed and any agreed advance payment is received. Informal requests, course of dealing, or Service Recipient instructions shall not expand the Services or Fees.', ('C-09','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §4.4.','Without a written change-order gate, Trident can expand scope informally and later contend the expanded work is included in the existing fee.','Firm on written dual signature and no obligation before execution. Cost-plus-10% is the fallback if Trident pushes back on the target markup.'))

187: p71=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 7.1 Service Provider Materials')
188: old71=p71.text
189: new71='Section 7.1 Service Provider Materials — Ownership; No License. Service Provider and its Affiliates retain all right, title, and interest in and to all Service Provider Materials, including tools, methodologies, templates, processes, software, systems, know-how, and processes, whether existing before or developed during the Term. No license, sublicense, right to use, right to copy, right to modify, right to create derivative works, or other interest in any Service Provider Materials is granted to Service Recipient by this Agreement, whether expressly, by implication, estoppel, or otherwise. Service Recipient may access and use Service Provider Materials only to the limited extent necessary to receive the Services during the applicable Service Period, and all such access shall cease upon expiration or termination. Any post-termination use requested by Service Recipient must be addressed in a separate written license agreement with separate consideration and appropriate restrictions.'
190: set_markup(p71,'Section 7.1 Service Provider Materials — Ownership; No License.',old71.split('. ',1)[1],new71.split('. ',1)[1])
191: add_comment(doc,p71,'CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','Andersen instructions; Playbook §6.1.','The draft grants a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free, sublicensable license to operational IP used across Polaris’s divisions, risking IP leakage and competitive harm.','Firm, board-level position: delete the license entirely. Any post-TSA tool access must be handled under a separate negotiated license with compensation and restrictions.')

193: p72=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 7.2 Service Recipient Materials.')
194: old72=p72.text
195: new72='Section 7.2 Data Ownership and Return. Service Recipient retains ownership of data relating exclusively to the Business that is provided to or generated for Service Recipient after Closing (Buyer Data). Service Provider retains ownership of all Service Provider systems, infrastructure, tools, methodologies, security data, system-level data, pre-Closing data, and data relating to Polaris or its other businesses. Service Provider shall use Buyer Data only to perform the Services and shall reasonably cooperate in exporting Buyer Data in a commonly used machine-readable format at the end of the applicable Service Period, subject to payment of accrued Fees and reasonable transition charges. Neither Party is required to disclose or transfer the other Party\'s proprietary information or any data that cannot lawfully be transferred.'
196: set_markup(p72,'Section 7.2 Data Ownership and Return.',old72.split('. ',1)[1],new72.split('. ',1)[1])
197: add_comment(doc,p72,'SIGNIFICANT','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §6.2.','The draft treats all Trident-provided materials alike and does not reserve Polaris’s systems, pre-Closing data, system-level metadata, or proprietary information, potentially turning routine migration into a broader data-transfer obligation.','Accept reasonable Buyer Data migration, but preserve Polaris ownership and confidentiality of systems, pre-Closing data, and other-division data.')

199: p78=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 8.4 Data Privacy.')
200: old78=p78.text
201: new78='Section 8.4 Data Privacy. Each Party shall comply with all applicable data privacy and data protection laws in connection with its performance under this Agreement, including U.S. laws and, to the extent applicable to processing involving individuals in Mexico, Mexico\'s Federal Law on Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties (Ley Federal de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de los Particulares, or LFPDPPP) and its Regulations. Each Party shall implement and maintain appropriate technical and organizational measures to protect personal data against unauthorized access, use, disclosure, alteration, or destruction.'
202: set_markup(p78,'Section 8.4 Data Privacy.',old78.split('. ',1)[1],new78.split('. ',1)[1])
203: add_comment(doc,p78,'CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','APA §7.12(g); Playbook §6.3; Andersen instructions.','The draft references only U.S. privacy law even though Polaris will process personal data for 300+ Mexican employees; this creates LFPDPPP compliance, consent, transfer, and enforcement risk.','Firm that the TSA must expressly cover LFPDPPP. The detailed allocation below is substantive and should be validated by Mexico/LatAm counsel before execution.')
204: add_insert_after(doc,p78,'Section 8.5 Mexico Data Processing Terms.', 'For Monterrey employee and other Mexico personal data: (a) Service Recipient is the data controller/responsible party and shall provide or cause to be provided compliant privacy notices (avisos de privacidad), obtain any required consents and authorizations for processing and cross-border transfers, and provide accurate, lawful instructions; (b) Service Provider is a processor/service provider and shall process such data only on documented instructions and only to perform the Services; (c) Service Provider shall maintain appropriate administrative, technical, and physical safeguards, restrict access to personnel with a need to know, and require equivalent obligations of Affiliates and subcontractors; (d) Service Provider shall notify Service Recipient without undue delay and, in any event, within seventy-two (72) hours after becoming aware of a security incident involving such data, and shall reasonably cooperate in investigation, mitigation, notices, and regulatory responses; (e) each Party shall assist the other with data-subject requests, audits, and legally required notices to the extent relevant to its role; and (f) upon expiration or termination, Service Provider shall return or securely delete such data at Service Recipient\'s direction, except to the extent retention is required by law, in which case it remains protected under this Article 8. The Parties shall execute any supplemental data-processing addendum reasonably required to document these terms.', ('C-10','CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','APA §7.12(g); Playbook §6.3; client instructions.','Without controller/processor allocation, privacy notices, cross-border transfer mechanics, safeguards, and breach cooperation, Polaris could be exposed to enforcement, employee claims, and operational disruption in Mexico.','Firm on allocation and core safeguards. Exact consent mechanics and addendum form should be confirmed by Mexico counsel; this is n... (line truncated to 2000 chars)

206: # indemnity
207: p82=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 9.1 Service Recipient Indemnification.')
208: old82=p82.text
209: new82='Section 9.1 Service Recipient Indemnification. Service Recipient shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Service Provider and its Affiliates and their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, successors, and assigns from and against Losses arising from third-party claims to the extent resulting from Service Recipient\'s use of or reliance on the Services, Service Recipient\'s breach of this Agreement, or the negligent or wrongful act or omission of Service Recipient or its personnel in connection with this Agreement, except to the extent the third-party claim results from Service Provider\'s gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct. The indemnity in this Section is subject to Section 10.1.'
210: set_markup(p82,'Section 9.1 Service Recipient Indemnification.',old82.split('. ',1)[1],new82.split('. ',1)[1])
211: add_comment(doc,p82,'SIGNIFICANT','SIGNIFICANT','APA §7.12(d); Playbook §5.3.','The draft covers direct first-party losses and broad breach/law theories, which can bypass the APA’s contemplated third-party indemnity structure and create uncapped exposure through carve-out arguments.','Firm on third-party-only scope and cap application; proportionate-fault wording may be a fallback.')
212: p83=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 9.2 Service Provider Indemnification.')
213: old83=p83.text
214: new83='Section 9.2 Service Provider Indemnification. Service Provider shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Service Recipient and its Affiliates and their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, successors, and assigns solely from and against Losses arising from third-party claims, but only to the extent such claims result from Service Provider\'s gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct in performing the Services. The indemnity in this Section is subject to Section 10.1 and does not create liability for ordinary negligence, a breach of this Agreement, or a violation of law unrelated to gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct.'
215: set_markup(p83,'Section 9.2 Service Provider Indemnification.',old83.split('. ',1)[1],new83.split('. ',1)[1])
216: add_comment(doc,p83,'CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','APA §7.12(d)(iii); Playbook §5.3.','The draft makes Polaris indemnify for any breach of covenant, representation, or law violation and does not limit the obligation to third-party claims, expanding the APA carve-out and threatening the agreed liability allocation.','Firm APA-compliance position: third-party claims only and gross negligence/fraud/willful misconduct threshold.')

218: p89=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 10.1 Aggregate Liability Cap.')
219: old89=p89.text
220: new89='Section 10.1 Aggregate Liability Cap. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, the aggregate liability of Service Provider and its Affiliates, and their respective officers, directors, employees, and agents, arising out of or related to this Agreement shall not exceed the total TSA Fees actually paid by Service Recipient to Service Provider during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the date on which the applicable claim is first asserted in writing by Service Recipient. During the first twelve (12) months after the Closing Date, the cap shall equal the TSA Fees actually paid from the Closing Date through the date the claim is first asserted in writing. The cap applies in the aggregate and not per claim. The limitation shall not apply to (i) a Party\'s fraud or willful misconduct, (ii) a Party\'s breach of its confidentiality obligations, or (iii) Service Provider\'s indemnification obligations for third-party claims, but only to the extent such claims result from Service Provider\'s gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct. This Section is intended to implement APA §7.12(d) and shall be construed accordingly.'
221: set_markup(p89,'Section 10.1 Aggregate Liability Cap.',old89.split('. ',1)[1],new89.split('. ',1)[1])
222: add_comment(doc,p89,'CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','APA §7.12(d); Andersen instructions; Playbook §5.1.','The draft uses 200% of all fees paid, creating a materially higher cap than the APA-required rolling 12-month fee cap and does not expressly cover Polaris Affiliates and personnel.','Firm, non-negotiable APA conflict. Illustrative exposure: draft at $1.139M/month for 18 months = $20.502M fees; 200% cap = $41.004M. APA cap after 12 months = $13.464M at corrected $1.122M/month; delta = $27.540M, or approximately 3.05x.')
223: 
224: p90=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 10.2 Consequential Damages.')
225: old90=p90.text
226: new90='Section 10.2 Consequential Damages. EACH PARTY HEREBY WAIVES, AND SHALL NOT ASSERT AGAINST THE OTHER PARTY, ANY AND ALL CLAIMS FOR CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, PUNITIVE, EXEMPLARY, OR INDIRECT DAMAGES, INCLUDING LOSS OF REVENUE, LOSS OF PROFITS, LOSS OF BUSINESS OPPORTUNITY, COST OF REPLACEMENT SERVICES, DIMINUTION OF VALUE, OR LOSS OF GOODWILL, ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT, REGARDLESS OF THEORY OR WHETHER ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY. This mutual waiver shall not limit liability for fraud or willful misconduct, breach of confidentiality, infringement or misappropriation of intellectual property, or third-party claims for which indemnification is available under Article 9, and shall apply notwithstanding failure of essential purpose of any remedy.'
227: set_markup(p90,'Section 10.2 Consequential Damages.',old90.split('. ',1)[1],new90.split('. ',1)[1])
228: add_comment(doc,p90,'CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','APA §7.12(d) requires a mutual waiver; Playbook §5.2; Andersen instructions.','The draft is one-way: Polaris waives claims against Trident but Trident does not waive consequential-damage claims against Polaris, leaving Polaris exposed to business-interruption and replacement-service damages.','Firm on mutuality. Narrow carve-outs for confidentiality, IP, and indemnified third-party claims are consistent with the playbook; fraud/willful misconduct may be retained.')
229: 
230: p97=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 12.1 Force Majeure.')
231: old97=p97.text
232: new97='Section 12.1 Force Majeure. Neither Party shall be liable for failure or delay caused by a Force Majeure Event beyond its reasonable control, including natural disasters, pandemics, war or terrorism, government action, sanctions or embargoes, strikes, power or telecommunications failures, internet outages, or cyberattacks. The affected Party shall promptly notify the other, use commercially reasonable mitigation efforts, and keep the other reasonably informed. Obligations are suspended, not terminated, during the event, and payment obligations accrued before the event remain due. If the Force Majeure Event continues for ninety (90) consecutive days and materially prevents performance of an affected Service, either Party may terminate that affected Service on written notice without penalty, subject to payment of accrued Fees and any agreed termination assistance.'
233: set_markup(p97,'Section 12.1 Force Majeure.',old97.split('. ',1)[1],new97.split('. ',1)[1])
234: add_comment(doc,p97,'SIGNIFICANT','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §10.1.','The draft excuses delay indefinitely but provides no exit if a prolonged outage makes continued performance impracticable or leaves Polaris bearing resource and reputational risk.','Target 90-day trigger; 120 days is the maximum fallback.')
235: 
236: p101=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 13.1 Service Recipient Insurance.')
237: old101=p101.text
238: new101='Section 13.1 Service Recipient Insurance. Service Recipient shall maintain during the Term and for twelve (12) months thereafter: (a) commercial general liability insurance of at least $5,000,000 per occurrence and $5,000,000 aggregate; (b) umbrella or excess liability insurance of at least $5,000,000; and (c) workers\' compensation insurance at statutory limits. Polaris and its Affiliates shall be named as additional insureds under the CGL and umbrella/excess policies, which shall include a waiver of subrogation in favor of Polaris and its Affiliates. Policies shall be issued by insurers rated at least A- by A.M. Best. Service Recipient shall deliver certificates and applicable endorsements within ten (10) Business Days after Closing and annually thereafter.'
239: set_markup(p101,'Section 13.1 Service Recipient Insurance.',old101.split('. ',1)[1],new101.split('. ',1)[1])
240: add_comment(doc,p101,'SIGNIFICANT','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §8.1.','The draft provides only $2M CGL and omits umbrella coverage, additional-insured protection, waiver of subrogation, workers’ compensation, and delivery timing, leaving Polaris exposed to industrial-operations claims.','Target $5M CGL + $5M umbrella and endorsements. $3M limits are the absolute fallback; do not waive umbrella or additional-insured status.')
241: 
242: p103=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 14.1 Audit Rights.')
243: old103=p103.text
244: new103='Section 14.1 Audit Rights. Service Recipient may, at its sole expense and no more than once in any twelve (12)-month period, audit Service Provider\'s books and records solely to verify Fees, upon at least thirty (30) Business Days\' prior written notice. Any audit shall occur during normal business hours, in a manner that does not unreasonably interfere with operations, and shall be conducted by Service Recipient or one independent auditor bound by confidentiality obligations reasonably satisfactory to Service Provider. The audit shall be limited to fee-related records for the audited period and shall exclude proprietary systems, internal cost methodologies, unrelated personnel records, privileged material, and information concerning other Polaris businesses. Service Recipient shall keep audit results confidential and shall not disclose them except to its Representatives with a need to know or as required by law.'
245: set_markup(p103,'Section 14.1 Audit Rights.',old103.split('. ',1)[1],new103.split('. ',1)[1])
246: add_comment(doc,p103,'SIGNIFICANT','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §9.1.','Two audits per calendar year at Polaris’s expense, with 10 business days’ notice and access to systems/personnel, is disruptive and invites fishing expeditions into proprietary information.','Target once per 12 months, 30 days, buyer expense, fee records only. Twice per TSA term / 20 days is the fallback.')
247: p104=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 14.2 Audit Adjustments.')
248: old104=p104.text
249: new104='Section 14.2 Audit Adjustments. If an audit shows an overcharge for the audited period exceeding five percent (5%), Service Provider shall credit the overcharge within thirty (30) days after written demand and reimburse Service Recipient\'s reasonable, documented audit costs. If the overcharge is five percent (5%) or less, Service Provider shall credit the overcharge but shall not be responsible for audit costs. If an audit shows an undercharge, Service Recipient shall pay the deficiency within thirty (30) days after Service Provider\'s written demand. Any interest shall be at the lesser of one percent (1%) per month or the maximum lawful rate.'
250: set_markup(p104,'Section 14.2 Audit Adjustments.',old104.split('. ',1)[1],new104.split('. ',1)[1])
251: add_comment(doc,p104,'SIGNIFICANT','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §9.1.','The draft makes Polaris pay audit interest and costs without a materiality threshold, incentivizing frequent or low-value audits.','Retain credit for any verified overcharge; reimburse audit costs only where the overcharge exceeds 5%.')
252: 
253: p105=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 15.1 Governing Law.')
254: old105=p105.text
255: new105='Section 15.1 Governing Law. This Agreement and all claims arising out of or relating to it shall be governed by the internal laws of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, without regard to conflict-of-laws principles that would require application of another jurisdiction\'s law.'
256: set_markup(p105,'Section 15.1 Governing Law.',old105.split('. ',1)[1],new105.split('. ',1)[1])
257: add_comment(doc,p105,'SIGNIFICANT','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §11.1; APA §12.3 permits the TSA to specify its governing law.','Ohio law gives Trident a home-state advantage despite Polaris’s Pennsylvania headquarters, personnel base, and counsel.','Target Pennsylvania law. Delaware is the fallback if required to match the APA; do not accept Ohio as the default.')
258: p106=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 15.2 Dispute Resolution.')
259: old106=p106.text
260: new106='Section 15.2 Dispute Resolution. Any dispute shall first be escalated to the Parties\' designated CFO- or General Counsel-level representatives, who shall have fifteen (15) Business Days to resolve it. Either Party may then request non-binding mediation. If unresolved, the dispute shall be finally resolved by confidential binding arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association under its Commercial Arbitration Rules, before one arbitrator with relevant industry experience, seated in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Judgment on the award may be entered in any court of competent jurisdiction. This Section does not limit either Party\'s right to seek temporary or injunctive relief to protect Confidential Information or intellectual property.'
261: set_markup(p106,'Section 15.2 Dispute Resolution.',old106.split('. ',1)[1],new106.split('. ',1)[1])
262: add_comment(doc,p106,'SIGNIFICANT','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §11.2.','Cuyahoga County litigation exposes Polaris to buyer-home-jurisdiction procedure, public dockets, broad discovery, and jury-waiver enforcement risk.','Target executive escalation, optional mediation, and AAA arbitration in Pittsburgh. Neutral venue or a three-arbitrator panel for disputes over $5M are negotiation fallbacks.')
263: 
264: p109=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 15.5 Entire Agreement.')
265: old109=p109.text
266: new109='Section 15.5 Entire Agreement; APA Precedence. This Agreement, its Schedules, the Purchase Agreement, and the other Transaction Documents constitute the entire agreement regarding their subject matter. In the event of conflict between this Agreement and the Purchase Agreement, the Purchase Agreement shall control unless this Agreement expressly states, with specific reference to the applicable provision of the Purchase Agreement, that the Parties intend to supersede that provision and each Party executes this Agreement with actual knowledge of the conflict. A general integration clause or general statement that this Agreement controls shall not supersede any APA provision. For the avoidance of doubt, the terms of APA §7.12 control where they impose a mandatory requirement on this Agreement.'
267: set_markup(p109,'Section 15.5 Entire Agreement; APA Precedence.',old109.split('. ',1)[1],new109.split('. ',1)[1])
268: add_comment(doc,p109,'CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','APA §12.5 requires APA supremacy absent a specific, express supersession reference and actual knowledge.','The draft’s broad exception could allow the TSA to override the APA without identifying the specific APA provision, undermining the binding 7.12 constraints and creating closing/post-closing dispute risk.','Firm: preserve APA supremacy and specific-reference requirement.')

add_comment(doc,p63,'C-08','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §4.3.','“Commercially reasonable time” is vague and weakens Polaris’s cash-flow protection; the draft also lacks late interest.','Target Net 30 / 1.5% per month. Net 45 and 1.0% per month are the playbook fallback positions.')
p64=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 6.4 Fee Escalation.')
old64=p64.text

new64='Section 6.4 Fee Escalation and Cost Changes. Subject to APA §7.12(b), on each anniversary of the Closing Date the estimated Fees shall be adjusted by the greater of (a) three percent (3%) or (b) the increase in CPI-U over the preceding twelve (12) months. In addition, Service Provider may propose an equitable adjustment for an Escalation Event, including a material increase in costs resulting from a change in law or regulation, vendor pricing, or a material increase in volume or scope requested by Service Recipient. Any adjustment remains subject to the APA\'s actual Fully-Loaded Cost and five-percent (5%) consent limitations.'
set_markup(p64,'Section 6.4 Fee Escalation and Cost Changes.',old64.split('. ',1)[1],new64.split('. ',1)[1])

add_comment(doc,p64,'SIGNIFICANT','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §4.2; APA §7.12(b) preserved by express savings language.','Fixed fees without a cost-change mechanism create a below-market incentive for Trident to delay migration and leave Polaris carrying inflation, regulatory, and vendor-cost risk.','Target greater of 3% or CPI-U plus Escalation Event; CPI-U only is the fallback. Any increase that implicates the APA five-percent threshold requires Buyer consent.')
p66=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 6.6 Disputed Amounts.')

add_insert_after(doc,p66,'Section 6.7 Change Orders.', 'Any request for services not expressly described in a Schedule, a material increase in volume, or a material change in scope shall be effective only through a written change order signed by authorized representatives of both Parties. Service Provider may accept or reject a requested change in its sole discretion. A change order shall specify scope, timing, assumptions, and pricing, which shall be cost plus fifteen percent (15%) unless otherwise agreed in writing; no work shall begin until the change order is fully executed and any agreed advance payment is received. Informal requests, course of dealing, or Service Recipient instructions shall not expand the Services or Fees.', ('C-09','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §4.4.','Without a written change-order gate, Trident can expand scope informally and later contend the expanded work is included in the existing fee.','Firm on written dual signature and no obligation before execution. Cost-plus-10% is the fallback if Trident pushes back on the target markup.'))
p71=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 7.1 Service Provider Materials')
old71=p71.text

new71='Section 7.1 Service Provider Materials — Ownership; No License. Service Provider and its Affiliates retain all right, title, and interest in and to all Service Provider Materials, including tools, methodologies, templates, processes, software, systems, know-how, and processes, whether existing before or developed during the Term. No license, sublicense, right to use, right to copy, right to modify, right to create derivative works, or other interest in any Service Provider Materials is granted to Service Recipient by this Agreement, whether expressly, by implication, estoppel, or otherwise. Service Recipient may access and use Service Provider Materials only to the limited extent necessary to receive the Services during the applicable Service Period, and all such access shall cease upon expiration or termination. Any post-termination use requested by Service Recipient must be addressed in a separate written license agreement with separate consideration and appropriate restrictions.'
set_markup(p71,'Section 7.1 Service Provider Materials — Ownership; No License.',old71.split('. ',1)[1],new71.split('. ',1)[1])

add_comment(doc,p71,'CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','Andersen instructions; Playbook §6.1.','The draft grants a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free, sublicensable license to operational IP used across Polaris’s divisions, risking IP leakage and competitive harm.','Firm, board-level position: delete the license entirely. Any post-TSA tool access must be handled under a separate negotiated license with compensation and restrictions.')
p72=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 7.2 Service Recipient Materials.')
old72=p72.text

new72='Section 7.2 Data Ownership and Return. Service Recipient retains ownership of data relating exclusively to the Business that is provided to or generated for Service Recipient after Closing (Buyer Data). Service Provider retains ownership of all Service Provider systems, infrastructure, tools, methodologies, security data, system-level data, pre-Closing data, and data relating to Polaris or its other businesses. Service Provider shall use Buyer Data only to perform the Services and shall reasonably cooperate in exporting Buyer Data in a commonly used machine-readable format at the end of the applicable Service Period, subject to payment of accrued Fees and reasonable transition charges. Neither Party is required to disclose or transfer the other Party\'s proprietary information or any data that cannot lawfully be transferred.'
set_markup(p72,'Section 7.2 Data Ownership and Return.',old72.split('. ',1)[1],new72.split('. ',1)[1])

add_comment(doc,p72,'SIGNIFICANT','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §6.2.','The draft treats all Trident-provided materials alike and does not reserve Polaris’s systems, pre-Closing data, system-level metadata, or proprietary information, potentially turning routine migration into a broader data-transfer obligation.','Accept reasonable Buyer Data migration, but preserve Polaris ownership and confidentiality of systems, pre-Closing data, and other-division data.')
p78=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 8.4 Data Privacy.')
old78=p78.text

new78='Section 8.4 Data Privacy. Each Party shall comply with all applicable data privacy and data protection laws in connection with its performance under this Agreement, including U.S. laws and, to the extent applicable to processing involving individuals in Mexico, Mexico\'s Federal Law on Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties (Ley Federal de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de los Particulares, or LFPDPPP) and its Regulations. Each Party shall implement and maintain appropriate technical and organizational measures to protect personal data against unauthorized access, use, disclosure, alteration, or destruction.'
set_markup(p78,'Section 8.4 Data Privacy.',old78.split('. ',1)[1],new78.split('. ',1)[1])

add_comment(doc,p78,'CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','APA §7.12(g); Playbook §6.3; Andersen instructions.','The draft references only U.S. privacy law even though Polaris will process personal data for 300+ Mexican employees; this creates LFPDPPP compliance, consent, transfer, and enforcement risk.','Firm that the TSA must expressly cover LFPDPPP. The detailed allocation below is substantive and should be validated by Mexico/LatAm counsel before execution.')

add_insert_after(doc,p78,'Section 8.5 Mexico Data Processing Terms.', 'For Monterrey employee and other Mexico personal data: (a) Service Recipient is the data controller/responsible party and shall provide or cause to be provided compliant privacy notices (avisos de privacidad), obtain any required consents and authorizations for processing and cross-border transfers, and provide accurate, lawful instructions; (b) Service Provider is a processor/service provider and shall process such data only on documented instructions and only to perform the Services; (c) Service Provider shall maintain appropriate administrative, technical, and physical safeguards, restrict access to personnel with a need to know, and require equivalent obligations of Affiliates and subcontractors; (d) Service Provider shall notify Service Recipient without undue delay and, in any event, within seventy-two (72) hours after becoming aware of a security incident involving such data, and shall reasonably cooperate in investigation, mitigation, notices, and regulatory responses; (e) each Party shall assist the other with data-subject requests, audits, and legally required notices to the extent relevant to its role; and (f) upon expiration or termination, Service Provider shall return or securely delete such data at Service Recipient\'s direction, except to the extent retention is required by law, in which case it remains protected under this Article 8. The Parties shall execute any supplemental data-processing addendum reasonably required to document these terms.', ('C-10','CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','APA §7.12(g); Playbook §6.3; client instructions.','Without controller/processor allocation, privacy notices, cross-border transfer mechanics, safeguards, and breach cooperation, Polaris could be exposed to enforcement, employee claims, and operational disruption in Mexico.','Firm on allocation and core safeguards. Exact consent mechanics and addendum form should be confirmed by Mexico counsel; this is n... (line truncated to 2000 chars)
# indemnity
p82=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 9.1 Service Recipient Indemnification.')
old82=p82.text

new82='Section 9.1 Service Recipient Indemnification. Service Recipient shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Service Provider and its Affiliates and their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, successors, and assigns from and against Losses arising from third-party claims to the extent resulting from Service Recipient\'s use of or reliance on the Services, Service Recipient\'s breach of this Agreement, or the negligent or wrongful act or omission of Service Recipient or its personnel in connection with this Agreement, except to the extent the third-party claim results from Service Provider\'s gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct. The indemnity in this Section is subject to Section 10.1.'
set_markup(p82,'Section 9.1 Service Recipient Indemnification.',old82.split('. ',1)[1],new82.split('. ',1)[1])

add_comment(doc,p82,'SIGNIFICANT','SIGNIFICANT','APA §7.12(d); Playbook §5.3.','The draft covers direct first-party losses and broad breach/law theories, which can bypass the APA’s contemplated third-party indemnity structure and create uncapped exposure through carve-out arguments.','Firm on third-party-only scope and cap application; proportionate-fault wording may be a fallback.')
p83=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 9.2 Service Provider Indemnification.')
old83=p83.text

new83='Section 9.2 Service Provider Indemnification. Service Provider shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Service Recipient and its Affiliates and their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, successors, and assigns solely from and against Losses arising from third-party claims, but only to the extent such claims result from Service Provider\'s gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct in performing the Services. The indemnity in this Section is subject to Section 10.1 and does not create liability for ordinary negligence, a breach of this Agreement, or a violation of law unrelated to gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct.'
set_markup(p83,'Section 9.2 Service Provider Indemnification.',old83.split('. ',1)[1],new83.split('. ',1)[1])

add_comment(doc,p83,'CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','APA §7.12(d)(iii); Playbook §5.3.','The draft makes Polaris indemnify for any breach of covenant, representation, or law violation and does not limit the obligation to third-party claims, expanding the APA carve-out and threatening the agreed liability allocation.','Firm APA-compliance position: third-party claims only and gross negligence/fraud/willful misconduct threshold.')
p89=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 10.1 Aggregate Liability Cap.')
old89=p89.text

new89='Section 10.1 Aggregate Liability Cap. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, the aggregate liability of Service Provider and its Affiliates, and their respective officers, directors, employees, and agents, arising out of or related to this Agreement shall not exceed the total TSA Fees actually paid by Service Recipient to Service Provider during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the date on which the applicable claim is first asserted in writing by Service Recipient. During the first twelve (12) months after the Closing Date, the cap shall equal the TSA Fees actually paid from the Closing Date through the date the claim is first asserted in writing. The cap applies in the aggregate and not per claim. The limitation shall not apply to (i) a Party\'s fraud or willful misconduct, (ii) a Party\'s breach of its confidentiality obligations, or (iii) Service Provider\'s indemnification obligations for third-party claims, but only to the extent such claims result from Service Provider\'s gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct. This Section is intended to implement APA §7.12(d) and shall be construed accordingly.'
set_markup(p89,'Section 10.1 Aggregate Liability Cap.',old89.split('. ',1)[1],new89.split('. ',1)[1])

add_comment(doc,p89,'CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','APA §7.12(d); Andersen instructions; Playbook §5.1.','The draft uses 200% of all fees paid, creating a materially higher cap than the APA-required rolling 12-month fee cap and does not expressly cover Polaris Affiliates and personnel.','Firm, non-negotiable APA conflict. Illustrative exposure: draft at $1.139M/month for 18 months = $20.502M fees; 200% cap = $41.004M. APA cap after 12 months = $13.464M at corrected $1.122M/month; delta = $27.540M, or approximately 3.05x.')
p90=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 10.2 Consequential Damages.')
old90=p90.text

new90='Section 10.2 Consequential Damages. EACH PARTY HEREBY WAIVES, AND SHALL NOT ASSERT AGAINST THE OTHER PARTY, ANY AND ALL CLAIMS FOR CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, PUNITIVE, EXEMPLARY, OR INDIRECT DAMAGES, INCLUDING LOSS OF REVENUE, LOSS OF PROFITS, LOSS OF BUSINESS OPPORTUNITY, COST OF REPLACEMENT SERVICES, DIMINUTION OF VALUE, OR LOSS OF GOODWILL, ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT, REGARDLESS OF THEORY OR WHETHER ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY. This mutual waiver shall not limit liability for fraud or willful misconduct, breach of confidentiality, infringement or misappropriation of intellectual property, or third-party claims for which indemnification is available under Article 9, and shall apply notwithstanding failure of essential purpose of any remedy.'
set_markup(p90,'Section 10.2 Consequential Damages.',old90.split('. ',1)[1],new90.split('. ',1)[1])

add_comment(doc,p90,'CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','APA §7.12(d) requires a mutual waiver; Playbook §5.2; Andersen instructions.','The draft is one-way: Polaris waives claims against Trident but Trident does not waive consequential-damage claims against Polaris, leaving Polaris exposed to business-interruption and replacement-service damages.','Firm on mutuality. Narrow carve-outs for confidentiality, IP, and indemnified third-party claims are consistent with the playbook; fraud/willful misconduct may be retained.')
p97=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 12.1 Force Majeure.')
old97=p97.text

new97='Section 12.1 Force Majeure. Neither Party shall be liable for failure or delay caused by a Force Majeure Event beyond its reasonable control, including natural disasters, pandemics, war or terrorism, government action, sanctions or embargoes, strikes, power or telecommunications failures, internet outages, or cyberattacks. The affected Party shall promptly notify the other, use commercially reasonable mitigation efforts, and keep the other reasonably informed. Obligations are suspended, not terminated, during the event, and payment obligations accrued before the event remain due. If the Force Majeure Event continues for ninety (90) consecutive days and materially prevents performance of an affected Service, either Party may terminate that affected Service on written notice without penalty, subject to payment of accrued Fees and any agreed termination assistance.'
set_markup(p97,'Section 12.1 Force Majeure.',old97.split('. ',1)[1],new97.split('. ',1)[1])

add_comment(doc,p97,'SIGNIFICANT','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §10.1.','The draft excuses delay indefinitely but provides no exit if a prolonged outage makes continued performance impracticable or leaves Polaris bearing resource and reputational risk.','Target 90-day trigger; 120 days is the maximum fallback.')
p101=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 13.1 Service Recipient Insurance.')
old101=p101.text

new101='Section 13.1 Service Recipient Insurance. Service Recipient shall maintain during the Term and for twelve (12) months thereafter: (a) commercial general liability insurance of at least $5,000,000 per occurrence and $5,000,000 aggregate; (b) umbrella or excess liability insurance of at least $5,000,000; and (c) workers\' compensation insurance at statutory limits. Polaris and its Affiliates shall be named as additional insureds under the CGL and umbrella/excess policies, which shall include a waiver of subrogation in favor of Polaris and its Affiliates. Policies shall be issued by insurers rated at least A- by A.M. Best. Service Recipient shall deliver certificates and applicable endorsements within ten (10) Business Days after Closing and annually thereafter.'
set_markup(p101,'Section 13.1 Service Recipient Insurance.',old101.split('. ',1)[1],new101.split('. ',1)[1])

add_comment(doc,p101,'SIGNIFICANT','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §8.1.','The draft provides only $2M CGL and omits umbrella coverage, additional-insured protection, waiver of subrogation, workers’ compensation, and delivery timing, leaving Polaris exposed to industrial-operations claims.','Target $5M CGL + $5M umbrella and endorsements. $3M limits are the absolute fallback; do not waive umbrella or additional-insured status.')
p103=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 14.1 Audit Rights.')
old103=p103.text

new103='Section 14.1 Audit Rights. Service Recipient may, at its sole expense and no more than once in any twelve (12)-month period, audit Service Provider\'s books and records solely to verify Fees, upon at least thirty (30) Business Days\' prior written notice. Any audit shall occur during normal business hours, in a manner that does not unreasonably interfere with operations, and shall be conducted by Service Recipient or one independent auditor bound by confidentiality obligations reasonably satisfactory to Service Provider. The audit shall be limited to fee-related records for the audited period and shall exclude proprietary systems, internal cost methodologies, unrelated personnel records, privileged material, and information concerning other Polaris businesses. Service Recipient shall keep audit results confidential and shall not disclose them except to its Representatives with a need to know or as required by law.'
set_markup(p103,'Section 14.1 Audit Rights.',old103.split('. ',1)[1],new103.split('. ',1)[1])

add_comment(doc,p103,'SIGNIFICANT','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §9.1.','Two audits per calendar year at Polaris’s expense, with 10 business days’ notice and access to systems/personnel, is disruptive and invites fishing expeditions into proprietary information.','Target once per 12 months, 30 days, buyer expense, fee records only. Twice per TSA term / 20 days is the fallback.')
p104=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 14.2 Audit Adjustments.')
old104=p104.text

new104='Section 14.2 Audit Adjustments. If an audit shows an overcharge for the audited period exceeding five percent (5%), Service Provider shall credit the overcharge within thirty (30) days after written demand and reimburse Service Recipient\'s reasonable, documented audit costs. If the overcharge is five percent (5%) or less, Service Provider shall credit the overcharge but shall not be responsible for audit costs. If an audit shows an undercharge, Service Recipient shall pay the deficiency within thirty (30) days after Service Provider\'s written demand. Any interest shall be at the lesser of one percent (1%) per month or the maximum lawful rate.'
set_markup(p104,'Section 14.2 Audit Adjustments.',old104.split('. ',1)[1],new104.split('. ',1)[1])

add_comment(doc,p104,'SIGNIFICANT','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §9.1.','The draft makes Polaris pay audit interest and costs without a materiality threshold, incentivizing frequent or low-value audits.','Retain credit for any verified overcharge; reimburse audit costs only where the overcharge exceeds 5%.')
p105=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 15.1 Governing Law.')
old105=p105.text

new105='Section 15.1 Governing Law. This Agreement and all claims arising out of or relating to it shall be governed by the internal laws of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, without regard to conflict-of-laws principles that would require application of another jurisdiction\'s law.'
set_markup(p105,'Section 15.1 Governing Law.',old105.split('. ',1)[1],new105.split('. ',1)[1])

add_comment(doc,p105,'SIGNIFICANT','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §11.1; APA §12.3 permits the TSA to specify its governing law.','Ohio law gives Trident a home-state advantage despite Polaris’s Pennsylvania headquarters, personnel base, and counsel.','Target Pennsylvania law. Delaware is the fallback if required to match the APA; do not accept Ohio as the default.')
p106=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 15.2 Dispute Resolution.')
old106=p106.text

new106='Section 15.2 Dispute Resolution. Any dispute shall first be escalated to the Parties\' designated CFO- or General Counsel-level representatives, who shall have fifteen (15) Business Days to resolve it. Either Party may then request non-binding mediation. If unresolved, the dispute shall be finally resolved by confidential binding arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association under its Commercial Arbitration Rules, before one arbitrator with relevant industry experience, seated in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Judgment on the award may be entered in any court of competent jurisdiction. This Section does not limit either Party\'s right to seek temporary or injunctive relief to protect Confidential Information or intellectual property.'
set_markup(p106,'Section 15.2 Dispute Resolution.',old106.split('. ',1)[1],new106.split('. ',1)[1])

add_comment(doc,p106,'SIGNIFICANT','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §11.2.','Cuyahoga County litigation exposes Polaris to buyer-home-jurisdiction procedure, public dockets, broad discovery, and jury-waiver enforcement risk.','Target executive escalation, optional mediation, and AAA arbitration in Pittsburgh. Neutral venue or a three-arbitrator panel for disputes over $5M are negotiation fallbacks.')
p109=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 15.5 Entire Agreement.')
old109=p109.text

new109='Section 15.5 Entire Agreement; APA Precedence. This Agreement, its Schedules, the Purchase Agreement, and the other Transaction Documents constitute the entire agreement regarding their subject matter. In the event of conflict between this Agreement and the Purchase Agreement, the Purchase Agreement shall control unless this Agreement expressly states, with specific reference to the applicable provision of the Purchase Agreement, that the Parties intend to supersede that provision and each Party executes this Agreement with actual knowledge of the conflict. A general integration clause or general statement that this Agreement controls shall not supersede any APA provision. For the avoidance of doubt, the terms of APA §7.12 control where they impose a mandatory requirement on this Agreement.'
set_markup(p109,'Section 15.5 Entire Agreement; APA Precedence.',old109.split('. ',1)[1],new109.split('. ',1)[1])

add_comment(doc,p109,'CRITICAL — MUST CHANGE','APA §12.5 requires APA supremacy absent a specific, express supersession reference and actual knowledge.','The draft’s broad exception could allow the TSA to override the APA without identifying the specific APA provision, undermining the binding 7.12 constraints and creating closing/post-closing dispute risk.','Firm: preserve APA supremacy and specific-reference requirement.')
p112=find_para_contains(doc,'Section 15.11 Interpretation.')

add_insert_after(doc,p112,'Section 15.12 Non-Solicitation of Service Provider Personnel.', 'During the Term and for twelve (12) months thereafter, Service Recipient shall not, directly or indirectly, solicit, recruit, hire, or engage any employee of Service Provider or its Affiliates who provided Services, without Service Provider\'s prior written consent. This restriction does not prohibit general solicitations not targeted at Service Provider personnel or hiring an individual whose employment was terminated by Service Provider without cause. The restriction applies to all service-providing personnel and is not limited to Schedule H.', ('C-20','SIGNIFICANT','Playbook §7.2.','The draft has no protection against Trident cherry-picking Polaris employees who gain detailed knowledge of the business and systems through the TSA.','Target 12 months after termination; six months is the fallback.'))

- Before circulation, confirm the attached redline's APA-conflict provisions with Sharon Petrosian and flag the IP-license deletion, liability-cap delta, and Mexico gaps as the issues for the May 1 status call.

- Use the playbook package as the second layer: staffing discretion, termination assistance, payment and change orders, fee escalation, audit limits, insurance, force-majeure termination, Pennsylvania/AAA arbitration, and non-solicitation.
